1	# Android MCP bridge design
2	
3	Kotlin MCP service, Jetpack Compose management UI and SQLite client configuration
4	
5	Design specification  •  27 October 2026  •  Architecture, catalog and reference implementation; Android runtime not deployed
6	
7	
8	# 1 Recommended design
9	
10	Build an Android application that maps the full declared Android binding surface, rather than a curated list of hand-written bindings, and exposes it through MCP. The Kotlin MCP server runs in a persistent foreground service independently of the UI, with optional start on boot. It exposes generated and schema-driven tools to on-device agents through authenticated loopback Streamable HTTP. Owner-paired ADB provides app-agnostic, on-demand rendered screen state and coordinate taps for uninstrumented Android apps. The calling agent decides when to poll, how to interpret pixels and where to tap; the bridge contains no app-specific workflows or scheduler. Public Android APIs, known Binder AIDL interfaces and optional Avalonia.RemoteControl cover narrower integrations. Jetpack Compose manages permissions through the Kotlin service; SQLite stores client, target, connection and logging configuration.
11	
12	At startup, resolve the running device's version-compatible bindings and types into an atomic view, retaining the complete inventory with unavailable/unknown reasons. Generic Binder invocation requires verified wire contracts and codecs plus the shared policy/admission gate; availability never grants authority.
13	
14	Expose a small stable discovery and invocation surface by default. Agents locate small functional tool groups for their job and activate coherent manifests within explicit context budgets. The complete catalog remains searchable. Catalog-driven callback registration returns a subscription handle and a bounded MCP resource journal, with explicit cancellation and local policies for synchronous callback replies; the callback and grouping contracts below extend this architecture without adding app-specific workflows.
15	
16	The bridge is a comprehensive binding gateway and a security boundary. Inventory completeness is separate from permission to invoke a binding. Native API and Binder calls use the bridge UID; authorized ADB commands normally use the Android shell identity. Neither preserves the MCP caller identity. Authenticate and authorize every client before dispatch. Effective authority is the intersection of bridge policy, adapter constraints and the selected backend’s actual Android authority. Root and hidden-API bypass are not assumed. A separately permissioned low-level Binder transaction interface exposes reachable endpoints without promising that Android will authorize every call.
17	
18	| Layer | Responsibility and boundary |
19	| --- | --- |
20	| On device MCP clients | Untrusted agent processes. A credential identifies a client; names and package headers do not. |
21	| Loopback transport | Authenticate each HTTP request, validate host and origin, enforce resource limits and isolate sessions. |
22	| Bridge application core | Validate typed arguments, evaluate policy, obtain request specific approval and admit execution. |
23	| Binding registry and executors | Generated SDK/AIDL/protocol inventory, generic invocation and optional low-level Binder transactions; ADB and Avalonia executors. Mapping is not a grant. |
24	| Android platform and services | Final OS permission checks, target application permissions and lifecycle constraints. |
25

28	
29	## Design commitments
30	
31	- Deny by default. A new tool, client or widened schema never inherits an Allow rule.
32	
33	- Deny, Ask and Allow are policy choices. OS unavailable is a separate observed capability state, not a fourth policy setting.
34	
35	- Expose the complete declared binding inventory with mapping and availability reasons. Per-client policy governs invocation, not whether a binding exists in the inventory.
36	
37	- Permission edits and revocation have a defined dispatch boundary; already dispatched irreversible work cannot be recalled.
38	
39	This is a proposed design, not a tested Android implementation. Section 2 lists compatibility gates; Section 19 defines the evidence required before shipping. Sections 14 to 18 specify per-client logging and authorized ADB/remote-control modes; the binding coverage and registry sections define comprehensive exposure. Sources identify platform facts; limits and component boundaries are design decisions.
40	
41	
42	# 2 Components and compatibility gates
43	
44	Use one Kotlin Android APK, application process and UID initially. A persistent foreground service owns the MCP listener and recovery state while the Compose activity owns presentation; closing the activity must not stop the server. The Compose activity uses a bounded unexported local Binder facade into the Kotlin service; both run in the same process and this is not a privilege boundary. Keep internal Android services and receivers unexported; any deliberately exported Binder entry point independently checks caller identity before async handoff. A separate service process is a later reliability option, not a privilege boundary by itself.
45	
46	| Proposed project | Contains | Must not contain |
47	| --- | --- | --- |
48	| bridge.domain (Kotlin) | Client identities, typed policy, canonical requests, decisions, revision values | Android or UI dependencies |
49	| bridge.application (Kotlin) | Pairing, policy changes, approvals, admission gate, audit coordination | Direct Binder transactions |
50	| bridge.protocol (Kotlin) | MCP mapping, paginated catalog and transport independent session dispatch | Permission decisions hidden in handlers |
51	| bridge.bindings (Kotlin runtime) | Offline-generated SDK/AIDL metadata ingestion, versioned schemas and generic marshalling; no runtime bytecode generation | Assumed schemas for unknown private services |
52	| bridge.storage.sqlite (Kotlin) | Repositories, migrations and transactional outbox | Raw bearer secrets |
53	| bridge.android (Kotlin) | Android lifecycle, Keystore, capability probes and native, ADB and optional Avalonia remote adapters | Policy bypass through reflection or raw dispatch |
54	| bridge.ui (Kotlin Compose) | Kotlin Compose views, ViewModels, local admin workflows | Direct SQL writes or implicit catalog-admin authority |
55	| bridge.tests (Kotlin plus offline tooling) | Pure policy tests, contract clients, fake adapters, Android instrumentation | Assumptions that mocks prove OS access |

60	## Baseline and release gates
61	
62	Both the MCP server and management UI are Kotlin by the user's latest decision. Use a Kotlin Android foreground service and Jetpack Compose Activity; pin a tested compatible Kotlin/Android/Compose package set. No .NET runtime is required by the bridge. Select minimum Android API and supported devices from product needs and current support tiers, not from a generic old template. [S1]
63	
64	| Gate | Evidence required before choosing packages or shipping |
65	| --- | --- |
66	| Android hosting | Kotlin release build runs an Android-compatible HTTP engine behind the Kotlin LoopbackHost interface, with pinned MCP wire contracts and bounded IO. No ASP.NET Core/Kestrel host is used. |
67	| MCP compatibility | Pin the 2025-11-25 wire baseline and a compatible SDK release after a real client exchange. Later SDK protocol revisions require a separate review; never mix initialization or session semantics. |
68	| SQLite native load | Use service-owned Android SQLite access with prepared statements and executable DDL. Prove constraints, triggers, migrations, transactions and catalog scale on every supported Android/ABI profile. [S2] |
69	| Persistent service | Prove truthful foreground service type, boot/start eligibility, notification behavior and restart recovery. Persistent hosting is required; an OS-blocked start is an explicit failure state, not a silent downgrade. [S3] |
70	| Trusted local endpoint | Prove paired server identity and credential setup in target MCP clients. TLS pinning and manual bearer support vary by client; do not silently downgrade. |

75	# 3 Transport and request lifecycle
76	
77	Compatibility target: MCP 2025-11-25 Streamable HTTP at one /mcp endpoint. This names a deliberate baseline, not a claim that it is the latest specification. Implement its initialization, protocol version negotiation, POST handling and optional GET SSE behavior as a coherent profile. Prefer the official protocol implementation behind an Android proven host adapter. [S4]
78	
79	
80	## Endpoint protections
81	
82	- Bind explicitly to 127.0.0.1 and, only if tested, ::1. Never 0.0.0.0, public interfaces or automatic remote tunneling. Validate Host against the bound endpoint; reject unexpected Origin values and all browser origins by default. An absent Origin is not authentication.
83	
84	- Authenticate every POST, GET, DELETE and SSE reconnection. A session identifier is not a credential. Bind sessions and event cursors to client, credential epoch and server boot identifier. Reject cross client session reuse.
85	
86	- Prefer paired loopback HTTPS with pinned bridge identity. Plain HTTP with a reusable bearer token has residual local port impersonation risk: another app can listen when the bridge is stopped. A bound before sharing ephemeral port helps but does not authenticate the server. If retained for compatibility, label this lower assurance mode and require explicit enablement; disable sensitive and state changing tools. Never disable certificate validation globally or install a system CA as a shortcut. Pairing trust is app specific and requires client support, so wire compatibility does not guarantee a drop in client setup.
87	
88	- Suggested initial limits: 256 KiB request body, JSON nesting 32, 4 active calls per client, 64 globally, bounded SSE queues and per client rate limits. Tune with tests; fail with explicit overload rather than unbounded memory growth.
89	
90	
91	## One tool call
92	
93	1. Parse a bounded UTF-8 JSON-RPC message; authenticate the transport credential and resolve the internal client record. Validate session ownership and negotiated protocol.
94	
95	1. Resolve the generated binding/tool ID and exact schema hash from the active versioned registry, or the explicitly scoped low-level transaction contract. Reject unknown fields, invalid types and out of range values. Materialize defaults before canonicalization.
96	
97	1. Resolve a validated invocation plan with binding ID, owned object/Binder handles, output fields, limits and service or ADB identity. Generic/raw calls use their own explicit schemas and scopes; caller-supplied transaction codes never bypass policy. SQL is never an execution transport.
98	
99	1. Evaluate current policy and Android capability. If Ask applies, suspend without dispatch and request local approval. Timeout, dismissal or absence of UI means no execution.
100	
101	1. Under the admission gate, recheck identity, revisions, scope, capability and approval; atomically consume one use approval and record execution admission. Dispatch outside the SQLite transaction.
102	
103	1. Invoke the adapter off the UI thread. Recheck before every subsequent effect or result emission; sanitize and bound output. Record a minimal outcome and return a normal MCP result or a sanitized error.
104	
105	
106	## Discovery and streams
107	
108	bindings.search/list/get expose every entry in the declared source coverage, including denied, unavailable and schema-unknown entries with reasons. Generated per-binding aliases appear in tools/list only in the opt-in dynamic alias mode defined in the functional-group section; binding.invoke provides a generic route to the same registry rather than requiring a giant tool prompt. If a client needs a filtered callable-tool view, keep the complete inventory separately accessible. Deny/Ask/Allow never removes a binding from the inventory, and discovery never grants execution. Pin cursors to registry/policy snapshots; reject stale cursors. Send negotiated list-change notifications after registry changes. SSE is transport, not a new subscription grant.
109	
110	
111	# 4 Pairing and client identity
112	
113	The authenticated principal is an immutable, random internal client_id resolved from a credential. MCP clientInfo.name, a display label, IP address, Android package text and user agent strings are untrusted metadata. HTTP alone cannot establish the calling Android package or UID. A copied bearer credential impersonates its owner; this is an explicit residual risk of the manual client profile.
114	
115	
116	## Manual pairing flow
117	
118	1. The owner opens Clients and selects Add client. The bridge creates an expiring pairing attempt in memory while its listener is already bound. Show endpoint, server identity fingerprint and a one time high entropy bootstrap secret; never use a short numeric code as the only credential.
119	
120	1. The owner enters this configuration in the intended agent. The agent proves possession of the bootstrap secret and presents a proposed label. The bridge UI displays a request fingerprint and identifies the label as client supplied. Require local confirmation before activation.
121	
122	1. Issue a cryptographically random per client bearer secret with at least 256 bits of entropy. Return it once over the authenticated pairing channel. The owner chooses a least privilege preset or starts with all tools denied. Pairing never grants all existing or future tools.
123	
124	1. Store only a verifier and nonsecret credential identifier. Consume the bootstrap secret on success; expire after a proposed two minute window or repeated failed attempts. If delivery fails, revoke the issued credential and pair again rather than redisplay it.
125	
126	Use an explicit pairing surface outside the MCP method catalog and enabled only during a local pairing window. Do not expose admin methods, policy mutation or token creation as agent tools. Manual preconfigured bearer authentication is an interoperability profile, not a claim of full MCP OAuth authorization compliance. A standards based authorization adapter may be added when target clients require it. [S5]
127	
128	
129	## Optional package aware pairing
130	
131	A dedicated, narrowly scoped Android pairing entry point can verify a real Binder calling UID and the associated signing identity. Do not accept the package name from request JSON. Resolve multi package UIDs, signing lineage and package changes deliberately. This grants no authority beyond owner approved policy; do not require it for generic MCP clients.
132	
133	
134	## Credential lifecycle
135	
136	| Action | Required effect |
137	| --- | --- |
138	| Rotate | Create a new credential and show it once. Owner may permit a short overlap. At its end, atomically revoke old, increment client epoch and move retained replacement to that epoch. Invalidate all client sessions and approvals. |
139	| Disable client | Persist disabled state and revision, cancel approvals and reject new admissions. Preserve policy for review; reenable requires local owner action. |
140	| Revoke | Persist revocation, increment credential epoch and close affected streams. Reuse is permanently rejected even if a client session remains open. |
141	| Restore backup | Restore client labels and rules as disabled templates only. Never restore active credentials, sessions, approvals or server identity. Require fresh pairing. |
142	
143	
144	
145	
146	# 5 Permission model and evaluation
147	
148	Use one policy evaluator over canonical binding identities and exact schema hashes, with Deny, Ask or Allow plus typed constraints. A required entry-point tool rule can only restrict binding authority. No wildcard tools, rule priorities, inherited Allow or regular expression permission language. Presets only populate explicit rules after preview; newly registered tools remain denied.
149	
150	| Order | Check | Result when it fails |
151	| --- | --- | --- |
152	| 1 | Valid credential, active client, bridge running | Reject; no capability or policy details to unauthenticated callers |
153	| 2 | Known binding or explicit low-level contract and accepted schema version | Unavailable or invalid tool |
154	| 3 | Global emergency deny or tool disabled | Deny, regardless of client choice |
155	| 4 | Every canonical binding has an exact schema-bound client rule and the entry-point rule exists; no rule denies | Deny by default |
156	| 5 | Arguments and requested output fit all scope constraints | Deny; Ask cannot expand the scope |
157	| 6 | Current backend authority, device state and target availability | OS unavailable; never treat Allow as an OS grant |
158	| 7 | Rule is Ask or global tool floor requires Ask | Require a valid one use request bound approval |
159	| 8 | Versions and capability still valid at admission | Admit, otherwise reevaluate or reject |
160	
161	
162	
163	
164	## Scope semantics
165	
166	Each adapter defines a closed constraint schema. Allowed resource identifiers and fields are exact sets; numeric caps are maximums; requested time ranges must fit the allowed interval. Within one rule all constraints are ANDed. Global, client and adapter bounds intersect. Empty sets mean no access, not unrestricted access. Unknown constraint keys or schema versions fail closed. Scope is evaluated on canonical resolved identifiers, never display strings or path prefix comparisons.
167	
168	Example: contacts.list may permit only displayName for selected contact identifiers, at most 20 rows and no phone or email fields. Requesting phone is denied, not silently upgraded to Ask. An approved document handle identifies one selected document and mode; a caller supplied content URI or filesystem path is not an equivalent grant. UI constraints and adapter enforcement use the same typed model.
169	
170	```
171	evaluate(principal, plan, snapshot):
172	  require active(principal) and currentCredential(principal)
173	  resolve generated, generic and known raw calls to identical canonical bindings
174	  reject known raw calls that cannot decode and validate the canonical arguments
175	  require a schema-bound binding rule for EVERY binding; absence or stale hash denies
176	  unknown raw calls require an explicit broad raw backend/service grant and tool rule
177	  collect binding rules, required entry-point rule and global/adapter guardrails
178	  if any deny or unknown semantics or arguments outside ANY constraint: DENY
179	  if not capabilityAvailableNow(plan): OS_UNAVAILABLE
180	  if any ask or globalAskFloor(plan): require validOneUseApproval(principal, plan, snapshot)
181	  recheck credential, registry/schema/target/policy versions at admission
182	  return ADMIT_CANDIDATE  // commit admission before dispatch
183	```
184	
185	
186	## Why capability inventory is separate
187	
188	Capability inventory records adapter presence, supported Android level, native permissions or ADB pairing state, AppOps/special access, hardware state, target binding health and check time. It is observed state, not policy. Store a diagnostic cache only; check required state again at execution. A permission callback or UI resume triggers refresh, but stale snapshots cannot guarantee a call will succeed. Native app grants and paired ADB shell authority are distinct; neither is root. Android remains the final authority. [S6]
189	
190	
191	# 6 Request specific approval
192	
193	Ask means approval of one prepared execution, not consent to an unbounded future conversation. The UI is a trusted local management surface, not a dialog rendered by the MCP client. Treat client names, arguments and returned service data as untrusted text. Do not let a tool result, deep link or notification action approve a request by itself.
194	
195	
196	## Approval binding
197	
198	Compute a versioned canonical digest after strict JSON validation, default insertion and typed resource resolution. Reject duplicate keys, nonfinite numbers and ambiguous encodings. Define deterministic object key ordering and numeric/string handling; preserve semantically significant text rather than normalizing it casually. Include all behavior affecting arguments and output filters, not just the tool name.
199	
200	```
201	approvalBinding = Hash(
202	  canonicalizationVersion, serverBootId, requestNonce,
203	  clientId, credentialEpoch, toolId, adapterSchemaVersion,
204	  canonicalArguments, resolvedResourceIds, targetIdentity,
205	  expectedResourceVersion, policyRevision, registryRevision,
206	  capabilityGeneration, monotonicExpiry
207	)
208	```
209	
210	Use a monotonic deadline within the current boot and a UTC timestamp only for display/audit. Proposed approval lifetime is 60 seconds, capped by the caller deadline. Wall clock rollback must not extend it. The raw arguments and any sensitive preview remain memory only. A changed resource version, target identity, policy revision or capability generation invalidates the approval and requires reevaluation.
211	
212	| State | Allowed transition |
213	| --- | --- |
214	| Pending | Approved, denied, expired, canceled or invalidated; no adapter call |
215	| Approved | Consumed once at admission if every binding still matches; otherwise invalidated |
216	| Consumed | Execution may begin; a retry cannot reuse this approval |
217	| Terminal | Denied, expired, canceled or invalidated cannot return to Approved |
218	
219	
220	
221	
222	## Interaction and race handling
223	
224	- Show client identity/fingerprint, exact action, recipient or resource, relevant values, requested output, side effect warning and expiry. Default focus is Deny. Allow once is separate from Edit policy; persistent permission changes use the normal Apply flow.
225	
226	- If the app is not in the foreground, use a privacy preserving notification that opens the app, subject to Android permission and background launch restrictions. Do not launch arbitrary activities silently. No available approval UI means expiry, not auto approval.
227	
228	- Keep the MCP request pending with bounded transport time and negotiated progress if available. No custom approval polling method is required for the baseline. If the request is canceled or times out before admission, cancel approval. Socket disconnection alone is not MCP cancellation; the original deadline still applies. [S4]
229	
230	- At admission, serialize approval consumption with revocation and policy commits. Atomically require status Approved and an exact revision match. Never hold a database transaction or a global lock while waiting for a human or while executing Binder work.
231	
232	
233	# 7 Revocation and Android lifecycle
234	
235	
236	## A precise execution boundary
237	
238	A single application admission coordinator orders permission commits, revocations and execution admissions. Under its short gate, persist the mutation or admission, update the immutable policy snapshot and signal affected work before releasing the gate. A policy commit must not acknowledge success while another thread can still admit against an old snapshot. SQLite serializes durable writes; the coordinator additionally orders in memory dispatch decisions.
239	
240	Define admission as the linearization point. Work admitted before revocation may already be in progress and can have irreversible effects. Recheck immediately before the adapter call to narrow the gap, but do not promise atomic revocation across a remote Binder service. Later steps in a multi step adapter need new checks. Prefer single effect adapters; require target supported transactions if a multi effect atomic operation is promised.
241	
242	| Situation | Behavior |
243	| --- | --- |
244	| Policy becomes narrower | Invalidate pending approvals; reevaluate queued calls and active output. Stop future disallowed effects and disclosures. Do not reuse cached discovery as authority. |
245	| Client revoked | Reject new requests and admission; cancel cooperatively, drop queued events, close its streams and prevent replay to the old principal. |
246	| Effect already dispatched | Attempt documented cancellation if safe. Record completed, canceled or outcome unknown honestly. Revocation is not rollback. |
247	| Connection reconnects | Authenticate again and validate ownership and revisions. Default v1 has no durable transport SSE replay; separately retained callback journals are read through resources/read; client retries cannot recreate an approval. |
248	
249	
250	
251	
252	## Persistent server requirement
253	
254	The MCP server must remain running independently of the Compose activity. Implement an Android foreground service with a persistent notification, explicit start/stop commands and a restart strategy such as START_STICKY where eligible. Persistence is the required operating mode, not an optional optimization. Android can still kill or restrict the process; there is no unconditional uptime guarantee on every device. WorkManager is not the listener host.
255	
256	Select a truthful foreground service type and meet its prerequisites. Evaluate specialUse with a declared subtype and any required distribution review, or connectedDevice only when the real use and prerequisites fit. Do not label an indefinite MCP server dataSync. Android background-start and boot restrictions remain release gates. A denied start exposes Error or Start requires owner action rather than pretending the server is running. [S3, S7]
257	
258	Persist desired_state running/stopped and start_on_boot separately from observed listener health. Start sets desired running; explicit Stop sets stopped before shutdown. A crash keeps desired running for recovery. START_STICKY recreation may supply a null Intent, so restore configuration from durable state rather than replaying the previous command. Keep stopWithTask disabled; task swipe and force-stop are different events. Stop closes admission/listeners, invalidates approvals, cancels supported work and releases only owned connections. Never turn a deliberate stop into an automatic restart.
259	
260	
261	# Service boot recovery and status indicators
262	
263	
264	## Optional boot start
265	
266	A manifest boot receiver reads only a minimal nonsecret boot preference, then requests eligible service startup; it does not perform database migrations or network work inline. Prefer full startup after user unlock, when credential-encrypted SQLite and Keystore material are available. Do not move client credentials, ADB keys or policy data into device-protected storage to bypass unlock. Persist a small boot preference mirror only, reconcile it with the authoritative configuration after unlock, and default off if inconsistent.
267	
268	Enable Start on boot only through local configuration. A prior manual Stop suppresses restart until Start is chosen again. Boot preference does not override force-stop, Android user-stopped state, device policy or denied foreground-service eligibility. A blocked or pre-unlock start is reported as Waiting for unlock or Start requires owner action. Android 15 limits BOOT_COMPLETED starts for several service types, including dataSync, camera, media playback, phone call, media projection and microphone; do not route around those limits. [S26]
269	
270	
271	## Independent server and backend health
272	
273	On recovery create a new boot ID, reopen and validate storage, restore policy, bind the authenticated endpoint, then report Running. Old sessions and approvals expire; admitted operations become interrupted or unknown and are never replayed. Reconnect ADB and Binder independently with bounded backoff and identity checks. The MCP server remains running even when self-ADB needs re-pairing or a target is offline; catalog entries report the backend unavailable.
274	
275	Keystore unavailability, migration failure or integrity failure cannot yield a permissive server. Remain paused or in an explicit error state with owner remediation. Binder death invalidates object handles and relevant approvals. ADB disconnect invalidates pending capture references and prevents new ADB admissions, but does not silently stop the MCP listener.
276	
277	
278	## AppBar and Android status icon
279	
280	Show a matching MCP server icon in the Compose top AppBar and the Android foreground-service notification/status bar. Derive both from actual listener readiness: Starting, Running, Stopping, Stopped or Error. Running begins only after bind and initialization succeed. ADB offline adds a separate backend warning while the MCP Running icon remains. Opening the notification shows server status; its explicit Stop action updates desired state before stopping and removes the foreground-service notification/icon. The in-app indicator changes to Stopped.
281	
282	Use a dedicated notification channel and Android monochrome small icon, with accessible text and no secret identifiers. Request notification permission where applicable. On Android 13+, denial can suppress the normal drawer/status-bar notification even though the foreground service appears in system task management; channel settings and system UI also control visibility. The app cannot guarantee or override the system icon when notifications are disabled. Keep in-app status truthful. [S27]
283	
284	Acceptance: close/rotate the activity without losing MCP service; kill the process and recover without replay; verify manual Stop and force-stop remain stopped; test reboot with boot enabled/disabled, pre-unlock and denied starts, listener bind failure, notification denial and ADB offline while MCP stays Running.
285	
286	
287	# 8 Kotlin Compose management interface
288	
289	Use one ComponentActivity hosting Jetpack Compose with ViewModel-held UI state and state hoisting. Navigation/saved state lives in ViewModels; platform concerns stay behind service-owned interfaces reached through the bounded local facade. Use a narrow phone layout below a proposed 720 device independent pixel breakpoint and a two pane layout above it; validate the breakpoint on actual devices and with large text.
290	
291	
292	## Wide layout permission editor
293	
294	| Clients | Client permissions for Research agent |
295	| --- | --- |
296	| Search clients | Active  •  fingerprint 6F2A  •  policy revision 18 |
297	| Research agent / Personal assistant / Test client | Permissions   Logging   Approvals   Connection |
298	| Add client / Disable client / Revoke credentials | Search all bindings  \|  Policy  \|  Mapping status |
299	
300	
301	
302	| Tool | Policy choice | Scope | Android status |
303	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
304	| screen.state | Deny  [Ask]  Allow | Whole display | ADB connected |
305	| settings.brightness.set | Deny  [Ask]  Allow | Raw range 16 to 240 / Manual mode only | Special access missing |
306	| document.read | [Deny]  Ask  Allow | No document handles | No selection |
307	| input.tap | [Deny]  Ask  Allow | Device wide input | ADB connected |
308	
309	
310	
311	Draft changes 2    Discard    Review and apply
312	
313	
314	## Phone layout without a compressed grid
315	
316	| Research agent | Permission detail |
317	| --- | --- |
318	| Search tools / Brightness write / Ask  •  OS access missing | Policy / Deny    [Ask]    Allow / Scope / Raw range 16 to 240    Edit |
319	| Device battery / Allow  •  Available | Android access / WRITE_SETTINGS not granted / Manage Android access |
320	| 2 draft changes | Discard    Review and apply |
321	
322	
323	
324	Wireframes are functional layouts, not final visual styling. On a phone, the detail pane is a separate page. Permission choices remain editable even while OS access is unavailable, but the UI states clearly that the rule cannot execute until Android access is separately granted. Granting Android permission never changes client policy.
325	
326	Use touch targets of at least a proposed 48 dp, text labels as well as colors, screen reader names, logical focus order and scalable text. Persist draft state across rotation without persisting secrets or pending approval payloads. Never place a real credential in clipboard automatically, diagnostic screenshots or notification text.
327	
328	
329	# 9 Editing and approval workflows
330	
331	
332	## Navigation and screen responsibilities
333	
334	| Screen | Primary content and actions |
335	| --- | --- |
336	| Overview | Runtime mode, endpoint identity, active sessions, approval count, capability issues and explicit Start or Stop. |
337	| Clients | Labels, credential fingerprints, active or disabled status, last seen metadata. Add, rotate, disable and revoke with clear consequences. |
338	| Permissions | Tool catalog, Deny Ask Allow controls, scope editor, effective policy explanation and separate OS capability state. |
339	| Approvals | Pending requests ordered by expiry. Open detail, review exact effect, Deny or Allow once; no bulk approval. |
340	| Logging and activity | Per-client Off/Metadata/Redacted diagnostic mode, expiry, quotas, purge/export and minimal audit. No raw payload inspection. |
341	| Settings | Persistent server health and AppBar icon, Start on boot, connections, notification settings, retention, export/restore and diagnostics. |
342	
343	
344	
345	
346	## Draft then apply
347	
348	1. Load client config with row_version and global policy_revision. Edits only change a local draft. Show a dirty indicator and warn before leaving. Inline scope validation uses the adapter schema.
349	
350	1. Review shows old and new decisions and scope deltas, especially widened resource sets, output fields and limits. Bulk changes require a per tool preview and cannot include future tools. Never bulk convert unavailable tools to Allow silently.
351	
352	1. Apply submits expected row_version and policy_revision to the application service. Inside one transaction, reject a mismatch; otherwise write rules, increment revisions, append minimal audit and outbox records. Under the admission gate install the new snapshot and invalidate approvals before acknowledging success.
353	
354	1. On conflict, show the latest saved state alongside the draft. The user may reload or explicitly reapply a reviewed merge. Never use last writer wins for permission grants. Read the committed state back through the application service to update the UI.
355	
356	
357	## Approval detail
358	
359	Example: “Research agent wants to read display names for 3 selected contacts. No phone numbers or email addresses will be returned. Permission policy revision 18. Expires in 42 seconds.” Show stable client fingerprint and selected resource summary. Ask the owner to unlock or authenticate locally for sensitive approvals if the chosen security profile requires it.
360	
361	Deny is immediate. Allow once is enabled only while the binding and deadline remain valid. If scope, resource revision or policy changes, replace the button with “Request changed — review again.” The UI must never rewrite the pending request and approve a different one. Closing the page does not approve anything.
362	
363	
364	## Android access and recovery
365	
366	Manage Android access opens an appropriate Android permission or settings flow through a platform abstraction while the activity is visible. Explain why it is needed and respect denial. Returning refreshes the capability inventory. Show remediation for denied permission, unavailable hardware, locked device, missing target service, unsupported OS and bridge stopped separately; do not collapse all into a gray Allow control.
367	
368	
369	# 10 SQLite schema and invariants
370	
371	Use one app private SQLite database for configuration and minimal durable state. Client, credential, execution and audit IDs are opaque random TEXT values; binding_id and entry_id are the same SHA-256 canonical source-signature identity defined in catalog/README.md, independent of source occurrence; timestamps are UTC integer milliseconds; revisions and epochs are nonnegative INTEGER values. All required fields are NOT NULL. Use explicit CHECK, UNIQUE and foreign key constraints; validate structured scope data in the application even if JSON checks are available.
372	
373	| Table and key | Fields and required constraints |
374	| --- | --- |
375	| clients / PK client_id | display_name; state CHECK active/disabled/revoked; credential_epoch >= 0; row_version >= 1; created_at; updated_at; last_seen_at nullable. Names are not unique identities. |
376	| credentials / PK credential_id | client_id FK clients RESTRICT; verifier BLOB length 32; kind CHECK mcp/admin; key_alias; state CHECK active/revoked; created_at; expires_at nullable; revoked_at nullable; epoch >= 0. UNIQUE(verifier). No raw tokens. |
377	| tools / PK tool_id | schema_version; adapter_version; capability_key; scope_schema_version; risk_class; registry_revision. binding associations through tool_binding_aliases; registry is generated from versioned sources. This table is a reconciled catalog, not executable imported code. |
378	| client_tool_rules / PK client_id, tool_id | client_id FK clients CASCADE; tool_id FK tools RESTRICT; tool_schema_version; effect CHECK deny/ask/allow; scope_json; scope_schema_version; updated_at. One exact rule per client/tool; schema mismatch is denied. |
379	| policy_state / PK singleton_id = 1 | policy_revision >= 1; registry_revision >= 1; emergency_deny CHECK 0/1; updated_at. Monotonic increments on every authorization relevant mutation. |
380	| tool_guardrails / PK tool_id | tool_id FK tools RESTRICT; disabled CHECK 0/1; require_ask CHECK 0/1; scope_json; scope_schema_version. These restrictions intersect client rules and cannot grant access. |
381	| executions / PK execution_id | client_id FK clients RESTRICT; credential_id FK credentials RESTRICT; tool_id FK tools RESTRICT; request_digest BLOB; boot_id; policy_revision; state CHECK admitted/dispatched/completed/failed/canceled/unknown; admitted_at; completed_at nullable; idempotency_key nullable. |
382	| audit_events / PK event_id | occurred_at; client_id nullable; tool_id nullable; operation; decision; reason_code; policy_revision; execution_id nullable; duration_ms nullable. No raw arguments, tokens, contacts or result text. |
383	| change_outbox / PK change_id | policy_revision; change_kind; affected_client_id nullable; created_at; delivered_at nullable. Written in the same transaction as policy changes; delivery is idempotent. |
384	| schema_migrations / PK version | checksum; applied_at. Exactly ordered migrations; app also checks PRAGMA user_version before opening the runtime. |
385	
386	
387	
388	Pending ordinary approvals, pairing attempts, MCP sessions and ordinary call arguments/results stay in memory and die on restart. The explicitly authorized bounded callback event journal and consumed registration-consent pins are functional storage exceptions defined below; they do not restore a pending owner approval or live OS registration. Optional allowlisted diagnostic projections follow Section 14, never raw payload persistence. Persist only redacted terminal approval events in audit_events. Keep revoked clients and credential tombstones until related executions age out; physical deletion is a separate retention operation, never a route to reenable old credentials.
389	
390	
391	# 11 Storage transactions and secret protection
392	
393	| Table and key | Additional configuration records |
394	| --- | --- |
395	| resource_grants / PK handle_id | client_id FK clients CASCADE; exact_uri_ciphertext; key_alias; modes CHECK read/write/read_write; enabled CHECK 0/1; revision >= 1; created_at. Index(client_id, enabled). Opaque per client handle; never a caller supplied URI. |
396	| bridge_config / PK singleton_id = 1 | row_version >= 1; desired_state CHECK running/stopped; start_on_boot CHECK 0/1; last_stop_reason nullable; fgs_type; transport_profile CHECK paired_tls/reduced_http; loopback_address; port_preference; server_identity_key_alias; retention_days >= 0; audit_size_cap > 0. No secret or private key bytes. |
397	
398	
399	
400	Persisted Android URI grants belong to the bridge app; resource_grants is the narrower per client mapping. Recheck the actual OS grant and exact document identity on each use. Scope never relies on URI prefix matching. Disable missing grants; after restore the owner reselects resources. Config or handle changes that affect authorization increment policy_revision under the same admission gate.

# Android MCP bridge design

Kotlin MCP service, Jetpack Compose management UI and SQLite client configuration

Design specification  •  27 October 2026  •  Architecture, catalog and reference implementation; Android runtime not deployed


# 1 Recommended design

Build an Android application that maps the full declared Android binding surface, rather than a curated list of hand-written bindings, and exposes it through MCP. The Kotlin MCP server runs in a persistent foreground service independently of the UI, with optional start on boot. It exposes generated and schema-driven tools to on-device agents through authenticated loopback Streamable HTTP. Owner-paired ADB provides app-agnostic, on-demand rendered screen state and coordinate taps for uninstrumented Android apps. The calling agent decides when to poll, how to interpret pixels and where to tap; the bridge contains no app-specific workflows or scheduler. Public Android APIs, known Binder AIDL interfaces and optional Avalonia.RemoteControl cover narrower integrations. Jetpack Compose manages permissions through the Kotlin service; SQLite stores client, target, connection and logging configuration.

At startup, resolve the running device's version-compatible bindings and types into an atomic view, retaining the complete inventory with unavailable/unknown reasons. Generic Binder invocation requires verified wire contracts and codecs plus the shared policy/admission gate; availability never grants authority.

Expose a small stable discovery and invocation surface by default. Agents locate small functional tool groups for their job and activate coherent manifests within explicit context budgets. The complete catalog remains searchable. Catalog-driven callback registration returns a subscription handle and a bounded MCP resource journal, with explicit cancellation and local policies for synchronous callback replies; the callback and grouping contracts below extend this architecture without adding app-specific workflows.

The bridge is a comprehensive binding gateway and a security boundary. Inventory completeness is separate from permission to invoke a binding. Native API and Binder calls use the bridge UID; authorized ADB commands normally use the Android shell identity. Neither preserves the MCP caller identity. Authenticate and authorize every client before dispatch. Effective authority is the intersection of bridge policy, adapter constraints and the selected backend’s actual Android authority. Root and hidden-API bypass are not assumed. A separately permissioned low-level Binder transaction interface exposes reachable endpoints without promising that Android will authorize every call.

| Layer | Responsibility and boundary |
| --- | --- |
| On device MCP clients | Untrusted agent processes. A credential identifies a client; names and package headers do not. |
| Loopback transport | Authenticate each HTTP request, validate host and origin, enforce resource limits and isolate sessions. |
| Bridge application core | Validate typed arguments, evaluate policy, obtain request specific approval and admit execution. |
| Binding registry and executors | Generated SDK/AIDL/protocol inventory, generic invocation and optional low-level Binder transactions; ADB and Avalonia executors. Mapping is not a grant. |
| Android platform and services | Final OS permission checks, target application permissions and lifecycle constraints. |




## Design commitments

- Deny by default. A new tool, client or widened schema never inherits an Allow rule.

- Deny, Ask and Allow are policy choices. OS unavailable is a separate observed capability state, not a fourth policy setting.

- Expose the complete declared binding inventory with mapping and availability reasons. Per-client policy governs invocation, not whether a binding exists in the inventory.

- Permission edits and revocation have a defined dispatch boundary; already dispatched irreversible work cannot be recalled.

This is a proposed design, not a tested Android implementation. Section 2 lists compatibility gates; Section 19 defines the evidence required before shipping. Sections 14 to 18 specify per-client logging and authorized ADB/remote-control modes; the binding coverage and registry sections define comprehensive exposure. Sources identify platform facts; limits and component boundaries are design decisions.


# 2 Components and compatibility gates

Use one Kotlin Android APK, application process and UID initially. A persistent foreground service owns the MCP listener and recovery state while the Compose activity owns presentation; closing the activity must not stop the server. The Compose activity uses a bounded unexported local Binder facade into the Kotlin service; both run in the same process and this is not a privilege boundary. Keep internal Android services and receivers unexported; any deliberately exported Binder entry point independently checks caller identity before async handoff. A separate service process is a later reliability option, not a privilege boundary by itself.

| Proposed project | Contains | Must not contain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bridge.domain (Kotlin) | Client identities, typed policy, canonical requests, decisions, revision values | Android or UI dependencies |
| bridge.application (Kotlin) | Pairing, policy changes, approvals, admission gate, audit coordination | Direct Binder transactions |
| bridge.protocol (Kotlin) | MCP mapping, paginated catalog and transport independent session dispatch | Permission decisions hidden in handlers |
| bridge.bindings (Kotlin runtime) | Offline-generated SDK/AIDL metadata ingestion, versioned schemas and generic marshalling; no runtime bytecode generation | Assumed schemas for unknown private services |
| bridge.storage.sqlite (Kotlin) | Repositories, migrations and transactional outbox | Raw bearer secrets |
| bridge.android (Kotlin) | Android lifecycle, Keystore, capability probes and native, ADB and optional Avalonia remote adapters | Policy bypass through reflection or raw dispatch |
| bridge.ui (Kotlin Compose) | Kotlin Compose views, ViewModels, local admin workflows | Direct SQL writes or implicit catalog-admin authority |
| bridge.tests (Kotlin plus offline tooling) | Pure policy tests, contract clients, fake adapters, Android instrumentation | Assumptions that mocks prove OS access |




## Baseline and release gates

Both the MCP server and management UI are Kotlin by the user's latest decision. Use a Kotlin Android foreground service and Jetpack Compose Activity; pin a tested compatible Kotlin/Android/Compose package set. No .NET runtime is required by the bridge. Select minimum Android API and supported devices from product needs and current support tiers, not from a generic old template. [S1]

| Gate | Evidence required before choosing packages or shipping |
| --- | --- |
| Android hosting | Kotlin release build runs an Android-compatible HTTP engine behind the Kotlin LoopbackHost interface, with pinned MCP wire contracts and bounded IO. No ASP.NET Core/Kestrel host is used. |
| MCP compatibility | Pin the 2025-11-25 wire baseline and a compatible SDK release after a real client exchange. Later SDK protocol revisions require a separate review; never mix initialization or session semantics. |
| SQLite native load | Use service-owned Android SQLite access with prepared statements and executable DDL. Prove constraints, triggers, migrations, transactions and catalog scale on every supported Android/ABI profile. [S2] |
| Persistent service | Prove truthful foreground service type, boot/start eligibility, notification behavior and restart recovery. Persistent hosting is required; an OS-blocked start is an explicit failure state, not a silent downgrade. [S3] |
| Trusted local endpoint | Prove paired server identity and credential setup in target MCP clients. TLS pinning and manual bearer support vary by client; do not silently downgrade. |




# 3 Transport and request lifecycle

Compatibility target: MCP 2025-11-25 Streamable HTTP at one /mcp endpoint. This names a deliberate baseline, not a claim that it is the latest specification. Implement its initialization, protocol version negotiation, POST handling and optional GET SSE behavior as a coherent profile. Prefer the official protocol implementation behind an Android proven host adapter. [S4]


## Endpoint protections

- Bind explicitly to 127.0.0.1 and, only if tested, ::1. Never 0.0.0.0, public interfaces or automatic remote tunneling. Validate Host against the bound endpoint; reject unexpected Origin values and all browser origins by default. An absent Origin is not authentication.

- Authenticate every POST, GET, DELETE and SSE reconnection. A session identifier is not a credential. Bind sessions and event cursors to client, credential epoch and server boot identifier. Reject cross client session reuse.

- Prefer paired loopback HTTPS with pinned bridge identity. Plain HTTP with a reusable bearer token has residual local port impersonation risk: another app can listen when the bridge is stopped. A bound before sharing ephemeral port helps but does not authenticate the server. If retained for compatibility, label this lower assurance mode and require explicit enablement; disable sensitive and state changing tools. Never disable certificate validation globally or install a system CA as a shortcut. Pairing trust is app specific and requires client support, so wire compatibility does not guarantee a drop in client setup.

- Suggested initial limits: 256 KiB request body, JSON nesting 32, 4 active calls per client, 64 globally, bounded SSE queues and per client rate limits. Tune with tests; fail with explicit overload rather than unbounded memory growth.


## One tool call

1. Parse a bounded UTF-8 JSON-RPC message; authenticate the transport credential and resolve the internal client record. Validate session ownership and negotiated protocol.

1. Resolve the generated binding/tool ID and exact schema hash from the active versioned registry, or the explicitly scoped low-level transaction contract. Reject unknown fields, invalid types and out of range values. Materialize defaults before canonicalization.

1. Resolve a validated invocation plan with binding ID, owned object/Binder handles, output fields, limits and service or ADB identity. Generic/raw calls use their own explicit schemas and scopes; caller-supplied transaction codes never bypass policy. SQL is never an execution transport.

1. Evaluate current policy and Android capability. If Ask applies, suspend without dispatch and request local approval. Timeout, dismissal or absence of UI means no execution.

1. Under the admission gate, recheck identity, revisions, scope, capability and approval; atomically consume one use approval and record execution admission. Dispatch outside the SQLite transaction.

1. Invoke the adapter off the UI thread. Recheck before every subsequent effect or result emission; sanitize and bound output. Record a minimal outcome and return a normal MCP result or a sanitized error.


## Discovery and streams

bindings.search/list/get expose every entry in the declared source coverage, including denied, unavailable and schema-unknown entries with reasons. Generated per-binding aliases appear in tools/list only in the opt-in dynamic alias mode defined in the functional-group section; binding.invoke provides a generic route to the same registry rather than requiring a giant tool prompt. If a client needs a filtered callable-tool view, keep the complete inventory separately accessible. Deny/Ask/Allow never removes a binding from the inventory, and discovery never grants execution. Pin cursors to registry/policy snapshots; reject stale cursors. Send negotiated list-change notifications after registry changes. SSE is transport, not a new subscription grant.


# 4 Pairing and client identity

The authenticated principal is an immutable, random internal client_id resolved from a credential. MCP clientInfo.name, a display label, IP address, Android package text and user agent strings are untrusted metadata. HTTP alone cannot establish the calling Android package or UID. A copied bearer credential impersonates its owner; this is an explicit residual risk of the manual client profile.


## Manual pairing flow

1. The owner opens Clients and selects Add client. The bridge creates an expiring pairing attempt in memory while its listener is already bound. Show endpoint, server identity fingerprint and a one time high entropy bootstrap secret; never use a short numeric code as the only credential.

1. The owner enters this configuration in the intended agent. The agent proves possession of the bootstrap secret and presents a proposed label. The bridge UI displays a request fingerprint and identifies the label as client supplied. Require local confirmation before activation.

1. Issue a cryptographically random per client bearer secret with at least 256 bits of entropy. Return it once over the authenticated pairing channel. The owner chooses a least privilege preset or starts with all tools denied. Pairing never grants all existing or future tools.

1. Store only a verifier and nonsecret credential identifier. Consume the bootstrap secret on success; expire after a proposed two minute window or repeated failed attempts. If delivery fails, revoke the issued credential and pair again rather than redisplay it.

Use an explicit pairing surface outside the MCP method catalog and enabled only during a local pairing window. Do not expose admin methods, policy mutation or token creation as agent tools. Manual preconfigured bearer authentication is an interoperability profile, not a claim of full MCP OAuth authorization compliance. A standards based authorization adapter may be added when target clients require it. [S5]


## Optional package aware pairing

A dedicated, narrowly scoped Android pairing entry point can verify a real Binder calling UID and the associated signing identity. Do not accept the package name from request JSON. Resolve multi package UIDs, signing lineage and package changes deliberately. This grants no authority beyond owner approved policy; do not require it for generic MCP clients.


## Credential lifecycle

| Action | Required effect |
| --- | --- |
| Rotate | Create a new credential and show it once. Owner may permit a short overlap. At its end, atomically revoke old, increment client epoch and move retained replacement to that epoch. Invalidate all client sessions and approvals. |
| Disable client | Persist disabled state and revision, cancel approvals and reject new admissions. Preserve policy for review; reenable requires local owner action. |
| Revoke | Persist revocation, increment credential epoch and close affected streams. Reuse is permanently rejected even if a client session remains open. |
| Restore backup | Restore client labels and rules as disabled templates only. Never restore active credentials, sessions, approvals or server identity. Require fresh pairing. |




# 5 Permission model and evaluation

Use one policy evaluator over canonical binding identities and exact schema hashes, with Deny, Ask or Allow plus typed constraints. A required entry-point tool rule can only restrict binding authority. No wildcard tools, rule priorities, inherited Allow or regular expression permission language. Presets only populate explicit rules after preview; newly registered tools remain denied.

| Order | Check | Result when it fails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Valid credential, active client, bridge running | Reject; no capability or policy details to unauthenticated callers |
| 2 | Known binding or explicit low-level contract and accepted schema version | Unavailable or invalid tool |
| 3 | Global emergency deny or tool disabled | Deny, regardless of client choice |
| 4 | Every canonical binding has an exact schema-bound client rule and the entry-point rule exists; no rule denies | Deny by default |
| 5 | Arguments and requested output fit all scope constraints | Deny; Ask cannot expand the scope |
| 6 | Current backend authority, device state and target availability | OS unavailable; never treat Allow as an OS grant |
| 7 | Rule is Ask or global tool floor requires Ask | Require a valid one use request bound approval |
| 8 | Versions and capability still valid at admission | Admit, otherwise reevaluate or reject |




## Scope semantics

Each adapter defines a closed constraint schema. Allowed resource identifiers and fields are exact sets; numeric caps are maximums; requested time ranges must fit the allowed interval. Within one rule all constraints are ANDed. Global, client and adapter bounds intersect. Empty sets mean no access, not unrestricted access. Unknown constraint keys or schema versions fail closed. Scope is evaluated on canonical resolved identifiers, never display strings or path prefix comparisons.

Example: contacts.list may permit only displayName for selected contact identifiers, at most 20 rows and no phone or email fields. Requesting phone is denied, not silently upgraded to Ask. An approved document handle identifies one selected document and mode; a caller supplied content URI or filesystem path is not an equivalent grant. UI constraints and adapter enforcement use the same typed model.

```
evaluate(principal, plan, snapshot):
  require active(principal) and currentCredential(principal)
  resolve generated, generic and known raw calls to identical canonical bindings
  reject known raw calls that cannot decode and validate the canonical arguments
  require a schema-bound binding rule for EVERY binding; absence or stale hash denies
  unknown raw calls require an explicit broad raw backend/service grant and tool rule
  collect binding rules, required entry-point rule and global/adapter guardrails
  if any deny or unknown semantics or arguments outside ANY constraint: DENY
  if not capabilityAvailableNow(plan): OS_UNAVAILABLE
  if any ask or globalAskFloor(plan): require validOneUseApproval(principal, plan, snapshot)
  recheck credential, registry/schema/target/policy versions at admission
  return ADMIT_CANDIDATE  // commit admission before dispatch
```


## Why capability inventory is separate

Capability inventory records adapter presence, supported Android level, native permissions or ADB pairing state, AppOps/special access, hardware state, target binding health and check time. It is observed state, not policy. Store a diagnostic cache only; check required state again at execution. A permission callback or UI resume triggers refresh, but stale snapshots cannot guarantee a call will succeed. Native app grants and paired ADB shell authority are distinct; neither is root. Android remains the final authority. [S6]


# 6 Request specific approval

Ask means approval of one prepared execution, not consent to an unbounded future conversation. The UI is a trusted local management surface, not a dialog rendered by the MCP client. Treat client names, arguments and returned service data as untrusted text. Do not let a tool result, deep link or notification action approve a request by itself.


## Approval binding

Compute a versioned canonical digest after strict JSON validation, default insertion and typed resource resolution. Reject duplicate keys, nonfinite numbers and ambiguous encodings. Define deterministic object key ordering and numeric/string handling; preserve semantically significant text rather than normalizing it casually. Include all behavior affecting arguments and output filters, not just the tool name.

```
approvalBinding = Hash(
  canonicalizationVersion, serverBootId, requestNonce,
  clientId, credentialEpoch, toolId, adapterSchemaVersion,
  canonicalArguments, resolvedResourceIds, targetIdentity,
  expectedResourceVersion, policyRevision, registryRevision,
  capabilityGeneration, monotonicExpiry
)
```

Use a monotonic deadline within the current boot and a UTC timestamp only for display/audit. Proposed approval lifetime is 60 seconds, capped by the caller deadline. Wall clock rollback must not extend it. The raw arguments and any sensitive preview remain memory only. A changed resource version, target identity, policy revision or capability generation invalidates the approval and requires reevaluation.

| State | Allowed transition |
| --- | --- |
| Pending | Approved, denied, expired, canceled or invalidated; no adapter call |
| Approved | Consumed once at admission if every binding still matches; otherwise invalidated |
| Consumed | Execution may begin; a retry cannot reuse this approval |
| Terminal | Denied, expired, canceled or invalidated cannot return to Approved |




## Interaction and race handling

- Show client identity/fingerprint, exact action, recipient or resource, relevant values, requested output, side effect warning and expiry. Default focus is Deny. Allow once is separate from Edit policy; persistent permission changes use the normal Apply flow.

- If the app is not in the foreground, use a privacy preserving notification that opens the app, subject to Android permission and background launch restrictions. Do not launch arbitrary activities silently. No available approval UI means expiry, not auto approval.

- Keep the MCP request pending with bounded transport time and negotiated progress if available. No custom approval polling method is required for the baseline. If the request is canceled or times out before admission, cancel approval. Socket disconnection alone is not MCP cancellation; the original deadline still applies. [S4]

- At admission, serialize approval consumption with revocation and policy commits. Atomically require status Approved and an exact revision match. Never hold a database transaction or a global lock while waiting for a human or while executing Binder work.


# 7 Revocation and Android lifecycle


## A precise execution boundary

A single application admission coordinator orders permission commits, revocations and execution admissions. Under its short gate, persist the mutation or admission, update the immutable policy snapshot and signal affected work before releasing the gate. A policy commit must not acknowledge success while another thread can still admit against an old snapshot. SQLite serializes durable writes; the coordinator additionally orders in memory dispatch decisions.

Define admission as the linearization point. Work admitted before revocation may already be in progress and can have irreversible effects. Recheck immediately before the adapter call to narrow the gap, but do not promise atomic revocation across a remote Binder service. Later steps in a multi step adapter need new checks. Prefer single effect adapters; require target supported transactions if a multi effect atomic operation is promised.

| Situation | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Policy becomes narrower | Invalidate pending approvals; reevaluate queued calls and active output. Stop future disallowed effects and disclosures. Do not reuse cached discovery as authority. |
| Client revoked | Reject new requests and admission; cancel cooperatively, drop queued events, close its streams and prevent replay to the old principal. |
| Effect already dispatched | Attempt documented cancellation if safe. Record completed, canceled or outcome unknown honestly. Revocation is not rollback. |
| Connection reconnects | Authenticate again and validate ownership and revisions. Default v1 has no durable transport SSE replay; separately retained callback journals are read through resources/read; client retries cannot recreate an approval. |




## Persistent server requirement

The MCP server must remain running independently of the Compose activity. Implement an Android foreground service with a persistent notification, explicit start/stop commands and a restart strategy such as START_STICKY where eligible. Persistence is the required operating mode, not an optional optimization. Android can still kill or restrict the process; there is no unconditional uptime guarantee on every device. WorkManager is not the listener host.

Select a truthful foreground service type and meet its prerequisites. Evaluate specialUse with a declared subtype and any required distribution review, or connectedDevice only when the real use and prerequisites fit. Do not label an indefinite MCP server dataSync. Android background-start and boot restrictions remain release gates. A denied start exposes Error or Start requires owner action rather than pretending the server is running. [S3, S7]

Persist desired_state running/stopped and start_on_boot separately from observed listener health. Start sets desired running; explicit Stop sets stopped before shutdown. A crash keeps desired running for recovery. START_STICKY recreation may supply a null Intent, so restore configuration from durable state rather than replaying the previous command. Keep stopWithTask disabled; task swipe and force-stop are different events. Stop closes admission/listeners, invalidates approvals, cancels supported work and releases only owned connections. Never turn a deliberate stop into an automatic restart.


# Service boot recovery and status indicators


## Optional boot start

A manifest boot receiver reads only a minimal nonsecret boot preference, then requests eligible service startup; it does not perform database migrations or network work inline. Prefer full startup after user unlock, when credential-encrypted SQLite and Keystore material are available. Do not move client credentials, ADB keys or policy data into device-protected storage to bypass unlock. Persist a small boot preference mirror only, reconcile it with the authoritative configuration after unlock, and default off if inconsistent.

Enable Start on boot only through local configuration. A prior manual Stop suppresses restart until Start is chosen again. Boot preference does not override force-stop, Android user-stopped state, device policy or denied foreground-service eligibility. A blocked or pre-unlock start is reported as Waiting for unlock or Start requires owner action. Android 15 limits BOOT_COMPLETED starts for several service types, including dataSync, camera, media playback, phone call, media projection and microphone; do not route around those limits. [S26]


## Independent server and backend health

On recovery create a new boot ID, reopen and validate storage, restore policy, bind the authenticated endpoint, then report Running. Old sessions and approvals expire; admitted operations become interrupted or unknown and are never replayed. Reconnect ADB and Binder independently with bounded backoff and identity checks. The MCP server remains running even when self-ADB needs re-pairing or a target is offline; catalog entries report the backend unavailable.

Keystore unavailability, migration failure or integrity failure cannot yield a permissive server. Remain paused or in an explicit error state with owner remediation. Binder death invalidates object handles and relevant approvals. ADB disconnect invalidates pending capture references and prevents new ADB admissions, but does not silently stop the MCP listener.


## AppBar and Android status icon

Show a matching MCP server icon in the Compose top AppBar and the Android foreground-service notification/status bar. Derive both from actual listener readiness: Starting, Running, Stopping, Stopped or Error. Running begins only after bind and initialization succeed. ADB offline adds a separate backend warning while the MCP Running icon remains. Opening the notification shows server status; its explicit Stop action updates desired state before stopping and removes the foreground-service notification/icon. The in-app indicator changes to Stopped.

Use a dedicated notification channel and Android monochrome small icon, with accessible text and no secret identifiers. Request notification permission where applicable. On Android 13+, denial can suppress the normal drawer/status-bar notification even though the foreground service appears in system task management; channel settings and system UI also control visibility. The app cannot guarantee or override the system icon when notifications are disabled. Keep in-app status truthful. [S27]

Acceptance: close/rotate the activity without losing MCP service; kill the process and recover without replay; verify manual Stop and force-stop remain stopped; test reboot with boot enabled/disabled, pre-unlock and denied starts, listener bind failure, notification denial and ADB offline while MCP stays Running.


# 8 Kotlin Compose management interface

Use one ComponentActivity hosting Jetpack Compose with ViewModel-held UI state and state hoisting. Navigation/saved state lives in ViewModels; platform concerns stay behind service-owned interfaces reached through the bounded local facade. Use a narrow phone layout below a proposed 720 device independent pixel breakpoint and a two pane layout above it; validate the breakpoint on actual devices and with large text.


## Wide layout permission editor

| Clients | Client permissions for Research agent |
| --- | --- |
| Search clients | Active  •  fingerprint 6F2A  •  policy revision 18 |
| Research agent / Personal assistant / Test client | Permissions   Logging   Approvals   Connection |
| Add client / Disable client / Revoke credentials | Search all bindings  \|  Policy  \|  Mapping status |



| Tool | Policy choice | Scope | Android status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| screen.state | Deny  [Ask]  Allow | Whole display | ADB connected |
| settings.brightness.set | Deny  [Ask]  Allow | Raw range 16 to 240 / Manual mode only | Special access missing |
| document.read | [Deny]  Ask  Allow | No document handles | No selection |
| input.tap | [Deny]  Ask  Allow | Device wide input | ADB connected |



Draft changes 2    Discard    Review and apply


## Phone layout without a compressed grid

| Research agent | Permission detail |
| --- | --- |
| Search tools / Brightness write / Ask  •  OS access missing | Policy / Deny    [Ask]    Allow / Scope / Raw range 16 to 240    Edit |
| Device battery / Allow  •  Available | Android access / WRITE_SETTINGS not granted / Manage Android access |
| 2 draft changes | Discard    Review and apply |



Wireframes are functional layouts, not final visual styling. On a phone, the detail pane is a separate page. Permission choices remain editable even while OS access is unavailable, but the UI states clearly that the rule cannot execute until Android access is separately granted. Granting Android permission never changes client policy.

Use touch targets of at least a proposed 48 dp, text labels as well as colors, screen reader names, logical focus order and scalable text. Persist draft state across rotation without persisting secrets or pending approval payloads. Never place a real credential in clipboard automatically, diagnostic screenshots or notification text.


# 9 Editing and approval workflows


## Navigation and screen responsibilities

| Screen | Primary content and actions |
| --- | --- |
| Overview | Runtime mode, endpoint identity, active sessions, approval count, capability issues and explicit Start or Stop. |
| Clients | Labels, credential fingerprints, active or disabled status, last seen metadata. Add, rotate, disable and revoke with clear consequences. |
| Permissions | Tool catalog, Deny Ask Allow controls, scope editor, effective policy explanation and separate OS capability state. |
| Approvals | Pending requests ordered by expiry. Open detail, review exact effect, Deny or Allow once; no bulk approval. |
| Logging and activity | Per-client Off/Metadata/Redacted diagnostic mode, expiry, quotas, purge/export and minimal audit. No raw payload inspection. |
| Settings | Persistent server health and AppBar icon, Start on boot, connections, notification settings, retention, export/restore and diagnostics. |




## Draft then apply

1. Load client config with row_version and global policy_revision. Edits only change a local draft. Show a dirty indicator and warn before leaving. Inline scope validation uses the adapter schema.

1. Review shows old and new decisions and scope deltas, especially widened resource sets, output fields and limits. Bulk changes require a per tool preview and cannot include future tools. Never bulk convert unavailable tools to Allow silently.

1. Apply submits expected row_version and policy_revision to the application service. Inside one transaction, reject a mismatch; otherwise write rules, increment revisions, append minimal audit and outbox records. Under the admission gate install the new snapshot and invalidate approvals before acknowledging success.

1. On conflict, show the latest saved state alongside the draft. The user may reload or explicitly reapply a reviewed merge. Never use last writer wins for permission grants. Read the committed state back through the application service to update the UI.


## Approval detail

Example: “Research agent wants to read display names for 3 selected contacts. No phone numbers or email addresses will be returned. Permission policy revision 18. Expires in 42 seconds.” Show stable client fingerprint and selected resource summary. Ask the owner to unlock or authenticate locally for sensitive approvals if the chosen security profile requires it.

Deny is immediate. Allow once is enabled only while the binding and deadline remain valid. If scope, resource revision or policy changes, replace the button with “Request changed — review again.” The UI must never rewrite the pending request and approve a different one. Closing the page does not approve anything.


## Android access and recovery

Manage Android access opens an appropriate Android permission or settings flow through a platform abstraction while the activity is visible. Explain why it is needed and respect denial. Returning refreshes the capability inventory. Show remediation for denied permission, unavailable hardware, locked device, missing target service, unsupported OS and bridge stopped separately; do not collapse all into a gray Allow control.


# 10 SQLite schema and invariants

Use one app private SQLite database for configuration and minimal durable state. Client, credential, execution and audit IDs are opaque random TEXT values; binding_id and entry_id are the same SHA-256 canonical source-signature identity defined in catalog/README.md, independent of source occurrence; timestamps are UTC integer milliseconds; revisions and epochs are nonnegative INTEGER values. All required fields are NOT NULL. Use explicit CHECK, UNIQUE and foreign key constraints; validate structured scope data in the application even if JSON checks are available.

| Table and key | Fields and required constraints |
| --- | --- |
| clients / PK client_id | display_name; state CHECK active/disabled/revoked; credential_epoch >= 0; row_version >= 1; created_at; updated_at; last_seen_at nullable. Names are not unique identities. |
| credentials / PK credential_id | client_id FK clients RESTRICT; verifier BLOB length 32; kind CHECK mcp/admin; key_alias; state CHECK active/revoked; created_at; expires_at nullable; revoked_at nullable; epoch >= 0. UNIQUE(verifier). No raw tokens. |
| tools / PK tool_id | schema_version; adapter_version; capability_key; scope_schema_version; risk_class; registry_revision. binding associations through tool_binding_aliases; registry is generated from versioned sources. This table is a reconciled catalog, not executable imported code. |
| client_tool_rules / PK client_id, tool_id | client_id FK clients CASCADE; tool_id FK tools RESTRICT; tool_schema_version; effect CHECK deny/ask/allow; scope_json; scope_schema_version; updated_at. One exact rule per client/tool; schema mismatch is denied. |
| policy_state / PK singleton_id = 1 | policy_revision >= 1; registry_revision >= 1; emergency_deny CHECK 0/1; updated_at. Monotonic increments on every authorization relevant mutation. |
| tool_guardrails / PK tool_id | tool_id FK tools RESTRICT; disabled CHECK 0/1; require_ask CHECK 0/1; scope_json; scope_schema_version. These restrictions intersect client rules and cannot grant access. |
| executions / PK execution_id | client_id FK clients RESTRICT; credential_id FK credentials RESTRICT; tool_id FK tools RESTRICT; request_digest BLOB; boot_id; policy_revision; state CHECK admitted/dispatched/completed/failed/canceled/unknown; admitted_at; completed_at nullable; idempotency_key nullable. |
| audit_events / PK event_id | occurred_at; client_id nullable; tool_id nullable; operation; decision; reason_code; policy_revision; execution_id nullable; duration_ms nullable. No raw arguments, tokens, contacts or result text. |
| change_outbox / PK change_id | policy_revision; change_kind; affected_client_id nullable; created_at; delivered_at nullable. Written in the same transaction as policy changes; delivery is idempotent. |
| schema_migrations / PK version | checksum; applied_at. Exactly ordered migrations; app also checks PRAGMA user_version before opening the runtime. |



Pending ordinary approvals, pairing attempts, MCP sessions and ordinary call arguments/results stay in memory and die on restart. The explicitly authorized bounded callback event journal and consumed registration-consent pins are functional storage exceptions defined below; they do not restore a pending owner approval or live OS registration. Optional allowlisted diagnostic projections follow Section 14, never raw payload persistence. Persist only redacted terminal approval events in audit_events. Keep revoked clients and credential tombstones until related executions age out; physical deletion is a separate retention operation, never a route to reenable old credentials.


# 11 Storage transactions and secret protection

| Table and key | Additional configuration records |
| --- | --- |
| resource_grants / PK handle_id | client_id FK clients CASCADE; exact_uri_ciphertext; key_alias; modes CHECK read/write/read_write; enabled CHECK 0/1; revision >= 1; created_at. Index(client_id, enabled). Opaque per client handle; never a caller supplied URI. |
| bridge_config / PK singleton_id = 1 | row_version >= 1; desired_state CHECK running/stopped; start_on_boot CHECK 0/1; last_stop_reason nullable; fgs_type; transport_profile CHECK paired_tls/reduced_http; loopback_address; port_preference; server_identity_key_alias; retention_days >= 0; audit_size_cap > 0. No secret or private key bytes. |



Persisted Android URI grants belong to the bridge app; resource_grants is the narrower per client mapping. Recheck the actual OS grant and exact document identity on each use. Scope never relies on URI prefix matching. Disable missing grants; after restore the owner reselects resources. Config or handle changes that affect authorization increment policy_revision under the same admission gate.
