1	# Verified design mechanisms after round013
2	
3	These mechanisms are normative for this revision and replace conflicting earlier wording. They are design contracts, not Kotlin implementation claims. The finding ledger retains all28 original findings, including the brightness claim refuted by the current official source.
4	
5	## Callback object construction and reachability
6	
7	CallbackDescriptor.materialization_strategy has closed values interface_dynamic_proxy, binder_generic_stub, prebuilt_adapter and unsupported_abstract_class. A public Java interface can use java.lang.reflect.Proxy with the exact source-proven interface list, declared methods and supported classloader. An AIDL callback uses a reviewed generic android.os.Binder subclass: attach/query the pinned descriptor, implement onTransact using the exact verified transaction IDs, flags and codecs, enforce interface tokens and sender UID/capability before handing off to the broker. Parcel/file-descriptor/Binder-handle lifetimes are bounded and released on every failure. This is not a universal AIDL compiler, non-SDK access bypass or arbitrary Binder-handle import.
8	
9	An abstract callback class cannot use java.lang.reflect.Proxy. It is registration-unsupported with ABSTRACT_CLASS_NO_RUNTIME_SUBCLASS unless a reviewed prebuilt Kotlin/Java subclass adapter is shipped and its adapter ID/version/hash and supported callback methods are pinned. No runtime dex/bytecode generation or downloaded executable code is selected. The catalog still identifies every abstract callback and its unknown/unreachable variants. SDK/Java invocation resolves public members at admission through java.lang.reflect or supported MethodHandles from the exact pinned JVM signature; do not ship hundreds of thousands of per-member wrappers. R8 keep rules preserve only reviewed bridge adapters and reflective entry points. Non-SDK/access failures are explicit NON_SDK_BLOCKED/OS_UNAVAILABLE reasons, never silently retried through a stronger identity.
10	
11	Permitted Binder-handle acquisition is (a) public bindService to an explicit exported component with package/signing identity verification, or (b) a handle returned by a documented public SDK handle-source method. Platform ServiceManager lookup and manager-private proxy fields are non-SDK; the ordinary app backend reports backend_unreachable:non_sdk instead of promising access. A separate ADB raw adapter may expose only reviewed fixed service-call operations supported by shell authority and its actual marshalling limits. That is not an app-UID IBinder handle, a generic verified Parcelable codec or permission to use hwbinder. Raw connection_id is either a real connection_profiles.profile_id or reserved platform:local; object handles pin that profile, user, target and backend epoch and cannot migrate between them. HIDL declarations and completion semantics remain inventory/classification. No ordinary app backend is assumed to access hwbinder; unsupported paths report backend_unreachable:hidl. A future separately reviewed privileged backend would require an explicit scope/design change, not an inferred owner grant.
12	
13	## Startup reuse and bounded admission
14	
15	A new boot invalidates old admission capabilities, process-local object handles and approvals. It does not require discarding a validated semantic selection cache. Reuse is allowed only if a fresh supported capability observation matches the cache's canonical semantic facts (platform/minor/extensions/build/OEM/module/interface identity and relevant availability), scope, inventory root, catalog/overlay generations, resolver/schema version and type-graph digest. Boot ID, observation time and transient handle IDs are excluded from that semantic key, but remain new runtime evidence. Verify the app-private cache seal against the Keystore-authenticated manifest, open the immutable generation and create a new view revision bound to the new boot/capability epoch; do not mutate/relabel the old view. File identity/generation and on-read page/document hashes detect stale/corrupt data; failure quarantines the cache and closes device admission. Root/full process compromise remains outside the stated trust guarantee. Every runtime permission/reachability/wire/handle check is fresh at dispatch regardless of cache reuse.
16	
17	For the API level35 (Android15) or later, 8GiB/128GB reference profile and approximately800k-entry inventory, proposed unmeasured p95 acceptance targets are <=600seconds for cold complete indexed resolution and <=10seconds for warm validated semantic reuse. Resolve in bounded batches, SQLite staging and indexed reverse-type worklists: application scratch<=64MiB, SQLite page cache<=64MiB, total service peak<=384MiB and disk scratch<=incoming catalog size. A large dependency closure that exceeds a bound spills to validated SQLite worklists or fails explicitly; it is not silently cut. Recompute affected closures on capability change, and perform full cold rebuild when compatibility keys or dependency provenance are insufficient. While Resolving, only authenticated policy/status, callback.status/callback.cancel and bindings.search/list/get are admitted; discovery reports resolving applicability. Device-affecting calls return VIEW_RESOLVING. Progress and cancellation remain bounded; the listener may be ready while device admission is unavailable, with separate status fields. These targets need real Android benchmarks; the historical Python4.30GiB/565.6second probe does not satisfy them.
18	
19	## Catalog delivery and management API ownership
20	
21	Large catalog delivery uses an owner-selected Storage Access Framework content URI, not the256KiB JSON request body. BridgeService obtains the owner-granted read capability, preflights capacity, streams bounded copy chunks into a new app-private staging file, hashes the exact copied bytes and fsyncs before matching the independently trusted manifest size/SHA. Only then open the SQLite input read-only for schema/integrity/FK/content validation and atomic activation. Untrusted filenames, archive paths or SQL are never commands. A bounded expiring staged-local-handle identifies this verified copy; POST /v1/catalog/imports carries that handle plus expected pins/idempotency key. An ADB-pushed file is usable only when the owner exposes it through this same supported URI flow; the app does not assume access to /data/local/tmp or another UID's private directory. Abort/quarantine incomplete or mismatched copies and never activate them.
22	
23	BridgeService owns the optional /v1/catalog administration route on the same authenticated loopback listener as /mcp, with separate route authorization. It is disabled by default and enabled only by fresh local owner action for a bounded maximum10-minute window. Owner-issued credentials.kind=admin are separate from kind=mcp; admin credentials are rejected by tools/call and ordinary MCP credentials are rejected by admin routes. Admin credential expiry cannot exceed the current management window, revocation closes active admin work before the commit boundary, and every import/mutation needs its exact owner authorization and CAS rules. The local Compose facade invokes the same application service without opening HTTP or minting an admin credential. No admin route is active merely because this design contains its specification. PUT/DELETE are the mutation family; no PATCH alias is defined.
24	
25	## Callback/group table and operation contracts
26	
27	These tables are additions to the service configuration model. Immutable version rows have append-only history and evidence; local override revisions remain separate from imported documents. Mandatory FK checking, unique indexes, scalar/check constraints and transactional publication follow the existing SQLite contract. JSON documents are schema-validated before commit; a CHECK on JSON text alone is insufficient. The executable migration/reference integration remains a phase deliverable to validate separately.
28	
29	| Table / key | Required constraints and indexes |
30	| --- | --- |
31	| callback_descriptors PK(callback_id, revision) | revision>=1; type_id and schema_hash pinned to immutable catalog revision; role CHECK proven_callback/candidate/proven_non_callback/unknown; materialization_strategy CHECK the four closed values above; evidence and unknown_reason; immutable document hash. Unknown/candidate cannot become registrable merely by a name heuristic. |
32	| callback_methods PK(callback_id, revision, method_id) | FK descriptor revision RESTRICT; method/schema/type closure pins; direction and async/sync/completion classification; optional prebuilt adapter and local reply-policy evidence. |
33	| callback_bindings PK(registration_binding_id, callback_id, callback_revision, formal_position) | position>=0; FK descriptor; exact registration and cleanup IDs/schema pins; token/receiver/argument mapping plus proven/unknown relationship state; unknown cleanup rejects reliable registration. |
34	| functional_groups PK(group_id, revision) | revision>=1; stable content hash; description/labels, source provenance and override lineage; schema/estimator version; descriptor byte cost>=0. Unassigned entries are indexed independently, never dropped. |
35	| group_memberships PK(group_id, revision, binding_id) | FK group revision RESTRICT; canonical binding and selected contract revision; lifecycle_unit_id; full type/dependency closure through versioned group_dependencies and type pins. Reject unresolved/cyclic/oversize activation instead of selecting part of a lifecycle unit. |
36	| group_activations PK(client_id, credential_epoch, mcp_session_id, activation_revision) | FK clients RESTRICT; revision>=1; owner/session/credential scope, catalog/device/policy epochs, complete desired group-hash set, byte/token-estimate limits and immutable view ETag. Active pointer update CAS; no cross-client cursor/view reuse. |
37	| subscriptions PK(subscription_id) | client_id FK clients RESTRICT; credential_epoch; stream_epoch; revision>=1; state CHECK registering/active/cancelling/closed/orphaned/outcome_unknown; registration/cleanup/schema/type/wire pins; consumed registration-consent record; lease_expires_at and approved_max_expiry; event/byte/inline/read quotas>0; accepted/durable/loss cursors; cleanup outcome. Index(client_id,state,lease_expires_at). |

# Verified design mechanisms after round013

These mechanisms are normative for this revision and replace conflicting earlier wording. They are design contracts, not Kotlin implementation claims. The finding ledger retains all28 original findings, including the brightness claim refuted by the current official source.

## Callback object construction and reachability

CallbackDescriptor.materialization_strategy has closed values interface_dynamic_proxy, binder_generic_stub, prebuilt_adapter and unsupported_abstract_class. A public Java interface can use java.lang.reflect.Proxy with the exact source-proven interface list, declared methods and supported classloader. An AIDL callback uses a reviewed generic android.os.Binder subclass: attach/query the pinned descriptor, implement onTransact using the exact verified transaction IDs, flags and codecs, enforce interface tokens and sender UID/capability before handing off to the broker. Parcel/file-descriptor/Binder-handle lifetimes are bounded and released on every failure. This is not a universal AIDL compiler, non-SDK access bypass or arbitrary Binder-handle import.

An abstract callback class cannot use java.lang.reflect.Proxy. It is registration-unsupported with ABSTRACT_CLASS_NO_RUNTIME_SUBCLASS unless a reviewed prebuilt Kotlin/Java subclass adapter is shipped and its adapter ID/version/hash and supported callback methods are pinned. No runtime dex/bytecode generation or downloaded executable code is selected. The catalog still identifies every abstract callback and its unknown/unreachable variants. SDK/Java invocation resolves public members at admission through java.lang.reflect or supported MethodHandles from the exact pinned JVM signature; do not ship hundreds of thousands of per-member wrappers. R8 keep rules preserve only reviewed bridge adapters and reflective entry points. Non-SDK/access failures are explicit NON_SDK_BLOCKED/OS_UNAVAILABLE reasons, never silently retried through a stronger identity.

Permitted Binder-handle acquisition is (a) public bindService to an explicit exported component with package/signing identity verification, or (b) a handle returned by a documented public SDK handle-source method. Platform ServiceManager lookup and manager-private proxy fields are non-SDK; the ordinary app backend reports backend_unreachable:non_sdk instead of promising access. A separate ADB raw adapter may expose only reviewed fixed service-call operations supported by shell authority and its actual marshalling limits. That is not an app-UID IBinder handle, a generic verified Parcelable codec or permission to use hwbinder. Raw connection_id is either a real connection_profiles.profile_id or reserved platform:local; object handles pin that profile, user, target and backend epoch and cannot migrate between them. HIDL declarations and completion semantics remain inventory/classification. No ordinary app backend is assumed to access hwbinder; unsupported paths report backend_unreachable:hidl. A future separately reviewed privileged backend would require an explicit scope/design change, not an inferred owner grant.

## Startup reuse and bounded admission

A new boot invalidates old admission capabilities, process-local object handles and approvals. It does not require discarding a validated semantic selection cache. Reuse is allowed only if a fresh supported capability observation matches the cache's canonical semantic facts (platform/minor/extensions/build/OEM/module/interface identity and relevant availability), scope, inventory root, catalog/overlay generations, resolver/schema version and type-graph digest. Boot ID, observation time and transient handle IDs are excluded from that semantic key, but remain new runtime evidence. Verify the app-private cache seal against the Keystore-authenticated manifest, open the immutable generation and create a new view revision bound to the new boot/capability epoch; do not mutate/relabel the old view. File identity/generation and on-read page/document hashes detect stale/corrupt data; failure quarantines the cache and closes device admission. Root/full process compromise remains outside the stated trust guarantee. Every runtime permission/reachability/wire/handle check is fresh at dispatch regardless of cache reuse.

For the API level35 (Android15) or later, 8GiB/128GB reference profile and approximately800k-entry inventory, proposed unmeasured p95 acceptance targets are <=600seconds for cold complete indexed resolution and <=10seconds for warm validated semantic reuse. Resolve in bounded batches, SQLite staging and indexed reverse-type worklists: application scratch<=64MiB, SQLite page cache<=64MiB, total service peak<=384MiB and disk scratch<=incoming catalog size. A large dependency closure that exceeds a bound spills to validated SQLite worklists or fails explicitly; it is not silently cut. Recompute affected closures on capability change, and perform full cold rebuild when compatibility keys or dependency provenance are insufficient. While Resolving, only authenticated policy/status, callback.status/callback.cancel and bindings.search/list/get are admitted; discovery reports resolving applicability. Device-affecting calls return VIEW_RESOLVING. Progress and cancellation remain bounded; the listener may be ready while device admission is unavailable, with separate status fields. These targets need real Android benchmarks; the historical Python4.30GiB/565.6second probe does not satisfy them.

## Catalog delivery and management API ownership

Large catalog delivery uses an owner-selected Storage Access Framework content URI, not the256KiB JSON request body. BridgeService obtains the owner-granted read capability, preflights capacity, streams bounded copy chunks into a new app-private staging file, hashes the exact copied bytes and fsyncs before matching the independently trusted manifest size/SHA. Only then open the SQLite input read-only for schema/integrity/FK/content validation and atomic activation. Untrusted filenames, archive paths or SQL are never commands. A bounded expiring staged-local-handle identifies this verified copy; POST /v1/catalog/imports carries that handle plus expected pins/idempotency key. An ADB-pushed file is usable only when the owner exposes it through this same supported URI flow; the app does not assume access to /data/local/tmp or another UID's private directory. Abort/quarantine incomplete or mismatched copies and never activate them.

BridgeService owns the optional /v1/catalog administration route on the same authenticated loopback listener as /mcp, with separate route authorization. It is disabled by default and enabled only by fresh local owner action for a bounded maximum10-minute window. Owner-issued credentials.kind=admin are separate from kind=mcp; admin credentials are rejected by tools/call and ordinary MCP credentials are rejected by admin routes. Admin credential expiry cannot exceed the current management window, revocation closes active admin work before the commit boundary, and every import/mutation needs its exact owner authorization and CAS rules. The local Compose facade invokes the same application service without opening HTTP or minting an admin credential. No admin route is active merely because this design contains its specification. PUT/DELETE are the mutation family; no PATCH alias is defined.

Unknown/candidate cannot become registrable merely by a name heuristic. |

Keep these folders out of the portable archive; bootstrap verified dependencies into task-local caches first. The wrapper does not make a fresh cache magically offline-ready.

## Targets

Run ./gradlew --offline validateArchitecture generateArchitectureDiagrams generateUiAssets renderStoryboards verifyDesignDocs packageDesignDocs. The same invocation is used inside the pinned container with only this docs project mounted, NODE_BIN selecting a compatible existing read-only Node runtime, network disabled and no exposed ports. STRUCTURIZR_CLI defaults to the existing image's /usr/local/structurizr-cli/structurizr.sh. The README records the actual invocation and receipts once complete.

No diagram is sent to a public renderer and no Structurizr workspace is uploaded.

## Tooling and license

The internal ARC port's pinned source and exact field/enum contract are documented in the design. MIT package metadata was verified upstream; authoritative notices remain a pre-distribution gate for copied/translated schema/code. This package contains the derived design contract, not the upstream source archive or a Kotlin port. Gradle/Structurizr/PlantUML/Marp are build dependencies with their own licenses; the archive includes configuration and wrapper provenance, not downloaded distributions or node_modules.

## Bootstrap and actual isolated build

On a machine with Python3/npm and the pinned existing renderer image available, run python3 tooling/bootstrap.py. It downloads only checksum-recorded Gradle/PlantUML task dependencies and performs npm ci with the included Marp integrity lock, without lifecycle scripts or global installation. Java21/Graphviz come from the documented image; this is separate from any Android app installation. Offline use requires a populated wrapper distribution and Marp cache.

The validated environment uses the official Gradle wrapper in the existing digest-pinned Structurizr container, user1000, network none, no exposed ports, task directory mounted at /workspace and an existing compatible Node binary at /tool-node/node. Node26.8.2 requires libatomic.so.1; an existing host copy is mounted read-only in that ephemeral container, its hash retained in toolchain-lock.json. This is an environment dependency, not a hidden package installation. Other existing Java21/Node environments can use the same tasks with STRUCTURIZR_CLI and NODE_BIN set to verified local tooling. No task starts a public diagram server.

Execution and model/docs validation receipts are in validation/ in the archive. The portable ZIP omits .tools, .gradle-home, all source catalog data, reviewer receipts, old diagram outputs, Word/PDF and raster mockups.

"""Task-local build dependencies only; no host installation, settings or remote service."""
import pathlib,urllib.request,hashlib,json,zipfile,datetime
R=pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1];T=R/'.tools';T.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
def get(url):
 with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url,headers={'User-Agent':'Android-MCP-local-documentation-build'}),timeout=60) as r:return r.read()
pinned=json.loads((R/'toolchain-lock.json').read_text());rows=[]
def save(url,p,expected=None):
 raw=p.read_bytes() if p.exists() else get(url);digest=hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest();expected=expected or next((v['sha256'] for v in pinned['files'] if v['file']==str(p.relative_to(R))),None)
 if expected is None:raise ValueError('Unpinned build dependency '+p.name)
 if digest!=expected:raise ValueError('Checksum mismatch '+p.name)
 p.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);p.write_bytes(raw);rows.append(dict(file=str(p.relative_to(R)),url=url,size_bytes=len(raw),sha256=digest));return raw
version='8.14.3';url='https://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-'+version+'-bin.zip';expected=get(url+'.sha256').decode().strip().split()[0]
raw=save(url,T/('gradle-'+version+'-bin.zip'),expected)
with zipfile.ZipFile(T/('gradle-'+version+'-bin.zip')) as archive:
 for item in archive.infolist():
  target=(T/item.filename).resolve()
  if not target.is_relative_to(T.resolve()):raise ValueError('Unsafe build dependency path')
 archive.extractall(T)
for p in (T/('gradle-'+version)/'bin').iterdir():p.chmod(p.stat().st_mode|0o111)
base='https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gradle/gradle/v'+version+'/'
for name in ['gradlew','gradlew.bat','gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar']:save(base+name,R/name)
(R/'gradlew').chmod(0o755)
properties='distributionBase=GRADLE_USER_HOME\ndistributionPath=wrapper/dists\ndistributionUrl=https\\://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-'+version+'-bin.zip\ndistributionSha256Sum='+expected+'\nnetworkTimeout=10000\nvalidateDistributionUrl=true\nzipStoreBase=GRADLE_USER_HOME\nzipStorePath=wrapper/dists\n'
(R/'gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties').write_text(properties)
puml='1.2025.10';url='https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/net/sourceforge/plantuml/plantuml/'+puml+'/plantuml-'+puml+'.jar';save(url,T/('plantuml-'+puml+'.jar'))
(R/'toolchain-bootstrap-receipt.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(created_at=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),files=rows,original_lock_sha256=hashlib.sha256((R/'toolchain-lock.json').read_bytes()).hexdigest()),indent=2)+'\n');print(json.dumps(dict(files=len(rows),gradle=version,plantuml=puml,task_local_only=True)))

import subprocess,os
marp=R/'.tools/marp';marp.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
for original,target in [('marp-package.json','package.json'),('marp-package-lock.json','package-lock.json')]:
 import shutil
 shutil.copyfile(R/'tooling'/original,marp/target)
subprocess.run(['npm','--userconfig',os.devnull,'--cache',str(R/'.tools/npm-cache'),'ci','--prefix',str(marp),'--ignore-scripts','--no-audit','--no-fund'],check=True)

400	Persisted Android URI grants belong to the bridge app; resource_grants is the narrower per client mapping. Recheck the actual OS grant and exact document identity on each use. Scope never relies on URI prefix matching. Disable missing grants; after restore the owner reselects resources. Config or handle changes that affect authorization increment policy_revision under the same admission gate.
401	
402	
403	## Indexes and connection policy
404	
405	Index credentials(client_id, state), client_tool_rules(tool_id), executions(client_id, admitted_at), audit_events(client_id, occurred_at), audit_events(occurred_at) and change_outbox(delivered_at, change_id). Add a partial unique index on executions(client_id, tool_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL. Generate keys per intended operation, not per HTTP retry; reject reuse with a different request digest.
406	
407	Enable PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON for every connection and verify it. Use WAL on app private local storage, a bounded busy timeout, short transactions and a single application writer queue. Readers use short snapshots so they do not pin the WAL indefinitely. Start with synchronous=FULL for security relevant mutations; benchmark before changing durability. Schedule bounded checkpoints and monitor database, WAL and free disk sizes. [S8, S9]
408	
409	
410	## Permission commit and execution admission
411	
412	```
413	with admissionGate:
414	  BEGIN IMMEDIATE
415	  assert client.row_version == expectedClientVersion
416	  assert policy_state.policy_revision == expectedPolicyRevision
417	  validate entire proposed rule set
418	  write rules; increment client.row_version and policy_revision
419	  append audit_event and change_outbox
420	  COMMIT
421	  install new immutable snapshot; invalidate old approvals
422	  signal affected calls and streams
423	// Acknowledge Apply only after the gate has published the commit
424	```
425	
426	Execution admission uses the same gate: reevaluate the current snapshot, reserve/consume an in memory one use approval, insert the admitted execution and commit before dispatch. On persistence failure no call is issued; a reserved approval is invalidated rather than restored optimistically. Crash after commit but before or during Binder execution yields unknown, not automatic retry. SQLite cannot atomically commit a remote Android side effect.
427	
428	
429	# Secret protection and storage recovery
430	
431	
432	## Secrets and privacy
433	
434	For token format credential_id.secret, look up the nonsecret ID and compare a constant time HMAC-SHA-256 verifier of the full token with a nonexportable Android Keystore key. SQLite stores the verifier and key alias, never the token or HMAC key. Separate keys protect transport server identity and any encrypted metadata. Hardware backing is checked, not assumed; Keystore protects extraction but a compromised app process may still invoke its keys. [S10]
435	
436	Do not store caller secrets in SQLite connection strings, preferences, logs, analytics or crash attachments. Sensitive scope labels and identifiers may require application level encryption under a Keystore wrapped key, depending on threat model. Base SQLite is not encrypted by default. An encrypted provider is an additional dependency and deployment gate, not an implicit property of SQLite.
437	
438	
439	## Migrations and backup
440	
441	Pause the listener for migrations, check schema/version and available space, apply each transactional migration and record its checksum only on success. Run foreign key and integrity checks. If a migration fails or the schema is newer than supported, remain stopped with a recovery message; do not reset the database or weaken policy. Use SQLite backup APIs or a tested consistent export, never copy only the live .db while WAL is active. [S11]
442	
443	Exclude secrets, the live database and sidecars, approvals and sessions from both cloud backup and device transfer. Validate Android extraction rules on supported devices; allowBackup=false alone is not a universal device transfer guarantee. [S14] Export a versioned, integrity checked configuration package with scope review; encrypt exports containing private identifiers. Restore into a staging database, validate, preview changes, then activate atomically with all clients disabled, fresh revisions and fresh pairing. Keystore keys are not assumed portable.
444	
445	
446	# 12 Convenience tool contracts
447	
448	These convenience wrappers do not limit the exposed binding surface. Every generated binding also has a stable ID, exact schemas, provenance and dispatch contract. Tool annotations are not authorization. Generic calls validate method/schema identity and client-owned handles; the separately granted low-level Binder path validates its transaction contract. Hand-written wrappers are optional ergonomic layers, not the inventory authority.
449	
450	| Tool | Input and output | Adapter and policy |
451	| --- | --- | --- |
452	| settings.brightness.get | Input {}. Output rawValue observed int32 plus withinDocumentedRange; documented range1..255, mode manual/automatic and observedAt. | Settings.System wrapper. Read current value and mode; do not promise physical luminance or device independent perceived brightness. [S15] |
453	| settings.brightness.set | Input rawValue integer 1..255 and expectedMode manual. Output observed value or conflict. | Require Settings.System.canWrite special access (WRITE_SETTINGS), plus policy/Ask. Refuse automatic mode rather than silently changing it; no arbitrary setting keys. [S15] |
454	| sensors.list / sensors.read | List allowed sensor types only. Read: sensorHandle, rateHz and durationMs. Return bounded samples with units, timestamps and accuracy. | SensorManager wrapper; exact sensor allowlist, proposed cap 20 Hz and 5 seconds. Respect runtime permissions, foreground restrictions and device limits; unregister on finish, cancellation, revocation or failure. [S16] |
455	| device.battery.read | Input {}. Output levelPercent, isCharging and observedAt; omit fields not permitted by policy. | Public Android battery API wrapper. Read only; no custom AIDL needed. Available data depends on platform state. |
456	| contacts.list | Input contactIds[], fields[], limit 1..100. Output bounded records plus an opaque scoped cursor. | ContactsContract / ContentResolver wrapper; READ_CONTACTS plus selected ID/field scope. No raw query, projection or selection string. [S12] |
457	| document.read | Input documentHandle, offset and maxBytes. Output bounded content of an allowed media type. | Handle minted from an owner selected persisted URI grant; bind it to client, exact URI, access mode and revision. Never accept arbitrary file paths. |
458	| partner.status.read | Input accountHandle. Output a versioned status record. | Illustrative integration with a known partner AIDL service, explicit component and pinned signing identity. Requires a real partner contract; not an existing Android platform API. |
459	
460	
461	
462	
463	# Tool exchanges and result behavior
464	
465	
466	## Settings and sensor semantics
467	
468	Brightness write uses the documented raw 1 to 255 range, with a narrower default policy range such as 16 to 240. Check manual mode before dispatch and read back afterward; Settings.System does not provide an atomic compare and set across external actors. Do not change automatic mode or undo another actor’s change. Report a conflict or uncertain outcome honestly. Sensor rates are requested ceilings, not promised delivery timing; bound sample count and bytes, report actual timestamps, and always unregister listeners. [S15, S16]
469	
470	
471	## Example MCP exchange
472	
473	```
474	POST /mcp
475	Authorization: Bearer <credential_id.secret>
476	MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-11-25
477	Mcp-Session-Id: <required-initialized-owned-session>
478	Content-Type: application/json
479	Accept: application/json, text/event-stream
480	
481	{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":42,"method":"tools/call",
482	 "params":{"name":"contacts.list","arguments":{
483	   "contactIds":["contact_7"],
484	   "fields":["displayName"],"limit":1}}}
485	
486	{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":42,"result":{
487	 "content":[{"type":"text","text":"1 contact returned"}],
488	 "structuredContent":{"contacts":[{
489	   "id":"contact_7","displayName":"Example person"}]},
490	 "isError":false}}
491	```
492	
493	This example assumes initialization, pairing, OS grant, scoped permission and any Ask approval already succeeded. The displayed contact is fictitious. Discovery advertises the matching output schema; the adapter validates and minimizes output before serialization. Cursors are opaque, client bound and invalidated by policy changes; they do not bypass field or row scope.
494	
495	
496	## Error contract and retries
497	
498	Use protocol errors for malformed or unsupported JSON-RPC/MCP requests; use a tool result with isError for a valid call that cannot execute, with stable sanitized codes such as POLICY_DENIED, APPROVAL_EXPIRED, OS_PERMISSION_REQUIRED, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED or OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. Authentication failures stay at HTTP. Never return stack traces, Binder parcels or existence details to unauthorized callers. Read retries may be safe; write retries require adapter supported idempotency or explicit user review.
499	
500	
501	# 13 Threat model and operational limits
502	
503	Protect user data, Android capabilities, approval integrity, credentials and policy history against malicious local apps, prompt injected agents, hostile websites reaching loopback, stolen client credentials and buggy target services. Device root or full bridge process compromise is outside the default trust guarantee; document this residual risk rather than implying Keystore or SQLite prevents it.
504	
505	| Threat | Required mitigation and residual limit |
506	| --- | --- |
507	| Confused deputy | Resolve client identity before dispatch; authorize exact tool, resource and output. Native services see the bridge UID; ADB uses shell authority, not the original MCP principal. |
508	| Local port impersonation | Pin paired server identity with HTTPS where supported. Do not claim random ports or localhost authenticate the bridge. Plain HTTP mode is reduced assurance. |
509	| DNS rebinding or browser attack | Loopback only binding, Host and Origin validation, no permissive CORS, no cookie auth, per request bearer verification. No browser page can pair silently. |
510	| Prompt injection or consent spoofing | Agent text cannot grant policy. Local UI renders escaped text, bounded previews and trusted action labels; approval is bound to an immutable canonical plan. |
511	| Credential theft or replay | High entropy secrets, Keystore backed verifier, short setup window, redaction, rotation and immediate revocation. Bearer possession remains impersonation until revoked. |
512	| Scope escape | Resolve exact resources, schema hashes and owned handles. Generic and raw Binder calls use the same per-client gate, bounded marshalling and service identity checks; no unvalidated pointer or SQL pass-through. |
513	| Revocation race | Serialized admission boundary, revision recheck, invalidated approvals, canceled streams and no stale replay. Cannot undo a previously dispatched external effect. |
514	| Memory or Binder denial of service | Bound request sizes, nested JSON, concurrent calls, pending approvals, output and event buffers. Use deadlines and bounded worker pools, not UI or Binder thread blocking. |
515	| Backup or diagnostic leakage | Private app storage, protected exports, no secrets or raw-payload logging, disabled clients after restore and opt in redacted diagnostics. |
516	| Database tampering or downgrade | Constrained schema, integrity checks, version checks and fail closed restore. App sandbox is the baseline; full OS compromise is not solved by these checks. |
517	
518	
519	
520	
521	## Logging and data retention
522	
523	Log opaque execution and client IDs, tool name, decision category, reason code, policy revision, latency and sanitized outcome. Never log Authorization headers, pairing secrets, full arguments, content URIs, contact names, document contents, raw Binder exceptions or SSE payloads. A request digest may itself enable correlation; retain only when needed, preferably keyed, and do not treat it as anonymous data.
524	
525	Optional call logging follows Section 14, with Off, Metadata and expiring Redacted diagnostic modes. Suggested mandatory audit default: 7 days of local redacted audit metadata and a fixed storage cap with owner controlled deletion. Configuration change audit should be durable; if it cannot be recorded, reject that mutation. For tool dispatch, failure to record admission fails closed. Logging is not tamper proof against full app compromise. Metrics and support exports are opt in and previewed before sharing.
526	
527	
528	# 14 Configurable call logging per client
529	
530	The local owner configures optional call logging independently for every authenticated client. Off means no optional call records, not zero security records: the minimal permission, revocation and execution-admission audit remains mandatory. A remote client cannot enable its own diagnostics, change retention or export logs.
531	
532	| Mode | Captured data and limits |
533	| --- | --- |
534	| Off | No optional call records. Mandatory minimal security/admission audit still applies. |
535	| Metadata default | Server-generated call ID, client ID, tool/backend ID, timestamps, duration, bounded decision/outcome code and revision numbers. No headers, targets, argument values or free-text errors. |
536	| Redacted diagnostic | Explicit per-client, time-limited opt-in. Add only adapter-defined, schema-validated derived fields such as counts, enum state and rounded timings. Redact before buffering. Never raw arguments, full results, screenshots, UI text, credentials, shell text or Binder parcels. |
537	
538	
539	
540	
541	## Logging tab and owner controls
542	
543	Clients > selected client > Logging shows mode, diagnostic expiry, retention, storage used/cap, per-record cap and dropped-record count. Proposed defaults: Metadata, 7-day retention, 10 MiB per client, 100 MiB total and a 4 KiB maximum diagnostic projection; a diagnostic session expires after 15 minutes. These are tunable design defaults, always bounded by global limits. Show a preview of the exact fields each tool may record before enabling diagnostics.
544	
545	Apply uses expected logging_revision, with the same draft/review/conflict experience as permissions. Pause stops future optional capture without deleting history. Purge optional logs deletes this client’s optional records and queued projections, not the security audit. Export is an explicit local-owner action over a bounded, redacted snapshot; warn that exported copies are outside later expiry or purge enforcement. RemoteControl and ADB input must not trigger these controls.
546	
547	
548	## SQLite extension
549	
550	| Table and key | Fields and invariants |
551	| --- | --- |
552	| client_logging_config / PK client_id | FK clients CASCADE; mode CHECK off/metadata/diagnostic; paused CHECK 0/1; logging_revision >= 1; retention_seconds >= 0; byte_quota >= 0; record_byte_cap >= 0; diagnostic_expires_at nullable; diagnostic_boot_id nullable; redaction_profile_version; updated_at. Diagnostic expires on restart. |
553	| client_call_logs / PK log_id | client_id FK clients CASCADE; call_id; tool_id; backend_kind; started_at; finished_at nullable; decision_code; outcome_code; policy_revision; logging_revision; expires_at; size_bytes >= 0; payload_ciphertext nullable; key_alias nullable. No raw payload columns. |
554	| logging_counters / PK client_id | FK clients CASCADE; optional_dropped_count >= 0; quota_dropped_count >= 0; last_drop_at nullable. Bounded aggregate counters, not one error row per failed log write. |
555	
556	
557	
558	Index client_call_logs(client_id, started_at), client_call_logs(expires_at) and client_call_logs(client_id, expires_at). Enforce each client quota and the global budget in the writer transaction; expire/evict oldest eligible optional records before rejecting new optional records. Keep a reserved, bounded budget for required security audit. Do not let a diagnostic flood consume all device storage.
559	
560	
561	# Logging lifecycle and failure semantics
562	
563	Keep logging_revision separate from authorization policy_revision. Ordinary logging changes do not broaden tool authority or invalidate otherwise unchanged Ask approvals. At request admission, capture the permitted logging ceiling; before every optional emission and commit, intersect that ceiling with current client settings and current global limits.
564	
565	```
566	effectiveCapture = admissionLoggingCeiling
567	                   INTERSECT currentClientLoggingConfig
568	                   INTERSECT currentGlobalLimits
569	// Enabling more capture affects new calls only.
570	// Reductions, expiry and revocation affect queued writes immediately.
571	```
572	
573	Enabling diagnostics during a call never reconstructs prior inputs or expands that call’s captured fields. Pausing, lowering the level, diagnostic expiry or client revocation suppresses further optional capture and discards now-disallowed buffers. Serialize queued writes against logging reductions so a stale snapshot cannot commit afterward. Shorter retention also reduces expiry of existing records; longer retention does not silently extend their original expiry.
574	
575	
576	## Security and data handling
577	
578	- Encrypt diagnostic projections with keys protected by Android Keystore. Use an independently destroyable per-client log-domain key if cryptographic deletion is required. Never reuse the mandatory-audit key for optional-log deletion. Plain SQLite is not encryption.
579	
580	- Adapter-defined allowlists are primary; regex redaction is only a secondary defense. Credentials, authorization headers, pairing codes, ADB private keys, target runtime tokens, clipboard/text input, UI text, file contents and screen images are always excluded, even when diagnostics are enabled.
581	
582	- Known authenticated denied calls may be attributed to that client and logged according to its settings, without denied argument values. Unauthenticated attempts have no trustworthy client ownership: use a separate rate-limited security aggregate, never an attacker-supplied client ID.
583	
584	- Log admitted, dispatched, completed, failed, canceled and outcome unknown distinctly. Admission does not prove a side effect happened. executions.state already includes dispatched; extend its diagnostic metadata and record dispatch time when observable; process death can still make the true outcome unknown.
585	
586	
587	## Failure and deletion behavior
588	
589	Optional logger failures drop bounded optional records and increment aggregate counters; they neither permit a denied action nor block an already authorized action merely to preserve diagnostics. Required pre-dispatch admission-audit failure remains fail closed for all execution admissions. A completion-audit failure after an irreversible effect cannot undo that effect: report the audit gap/unknown status and never reexecute solely to obtain a log.
590	
591	Purge must clear queued projections, committed rows, indexes/caches and prepared local exports. Ordinary SQLite deletion does not guarantee immediate physical erasure from WAL files, backups or flash storage. Checkpoint/vacuum policies and independently destroyable encryption keys address different risks; do not promise secure erasure without evidence.
592	
593	
594	## Logging acceptance checks
595	
596	Test client isolation; Off-to-diagnostic during a call; diagnostic-to-Off/expiry/revocation racing a queued write; secret canaries; per-client/global quota pressure; retention shortening; export review; purge versus mandatory audit; disk-full drop counting; and post-effect audit failure without duplicate execution.
597	
598	
599	# 15 Authorized ADB execution architecture
600	
601	The primary arbitrary-app control path is App A agent -> authenticated MCP bridge -> typed ADB adapter -> owner-paired adbd -> the visible UI of App B. App B does not need Avalonia or embedded instrumentation for on-demand screen.state and input.tap operations. Optional UI hierarchy is a separately permissioned capability, not a prerequisite. This is reusable visible-UI access, not private-data access or full debugging of every application.
602	
603	
604	## Three distinct backend modes
605	
606	| Mode | Connection and trust |
607	| --- | --- |
608	| Self ADB primary | An embedded/native ADB client connects from the bridge app to this device’s owner-enabled Wireless Debugging service. Android 11+ is the starting compatibility target, subject to device support. Owner explicitly enables and pairs it. LADB demonstrates feasibility, not a selected dependency or license approval. [S17, S18] |
609	| External ADB host | An already-authorized USB or securely paired wireless host forwards its localhost socket to a phone loopback endpoint. Keep the host ADB server and forwards local. This is separate from the same-device ADB client profile. [S19] |
610	| Avalonia runtime optional | A target app embeds an opted-in Avalonia.RemoteControl runtime. A new Android protocol adapter controls only its exposed Avalonia root. This specialized route is not required for arbitrary-app ADB automation. [S20] |
611	
612	
613	
614	MCP client identity, ADB paired-host identity and target-app identity are different principals. A paired ADB key establishes backend access, not a per-agent permission grant. Every MCP call still passes the bridge policy engine. Ordinary adbd commands use shell authority, not root and not the bridge UID. Device policy, user/profile boundaries, protected windows and platform restrictions remain upper bounds.
615	
616	
617	## Pairing and lifecycle
618	
619	1. In local Settings > Connections, create a Self ADB profile. Explain the broad shell authority and require the owner to enable Wireless Debugging and confirm its pairing code in Android settings. Never enable debugging, accept a pairing prompt or change security settings silently.
620	
621	1. Use the pairing endpoint only for pairing, then discover the authenticated connect endpoint. Ports may differ and change after reboot, debugging toggle or network changes. Track Unpaired, Paired offline, Connecting, Connected, Locked and Revoked separately.
622	
623	1. Persist the ADB key encrypted under a Keystore-protected wrapping key and exclude it from backup/export/logs. A native ADB implementation may need plaintext key material in process; do not claim the ADB private key is nonexportable or hardware backed unless proven.
624	
625	1. On disconnect, stop admissions that need ADB, cancel bounded collectors and mark dispatched unknown outcomes honestly. Reconnect with the same trusted profile only after endpoint rediscovery and peer verification; never fall back to unauthenticated tcpip 5555.
626	
627	Owner Disconnect pauses this connection. Revoke deletes local key material and requires Android-side revocation/forgetting of the paired identity to remove device trust fully. A stored local status must not claim the Android pairing was revoked without confirmation. Device reboot or force-stop recovery is best effort, not an always-on guarantee.
628	
629	
630	# ADB connection records and remote host loopback
631	
632	
633	## SQLite connection and target profiles
634	
635	| Table and key | Fields and required constraints |
636	| --- | --- |
637	| connection_profiles / PK profile_id | backend_kind CHECK self_adb/external_adb/avalonia_runtime; display_name; enabled CHECK 0/1; row_version >= 1; device_serial_or_binding nullable; android_user_id; endpoint_metadata_json; peer_fingerprint nullable; verification_strength; secret_ciphertext nullable; wrapping_key_alias nullable; paired_at nullable; revoked_at nullable. No plaintext key or token. |
638	| target_app_profiles / PK target_id | connection_profile_id FK connection_profiles RESTRICT; package_name; signing_identity nullable; identity_verification_method; runtime_protocol nullable; runtime_endpoint nullable; server_identity nullable; enabled CHECK 0/1; row_version >= 1. An HTTP/TCP package header is never verified identity. |
639	| Existing table extensions | tools.executor_kind CHECK native/adb/avalonia; executions.connection_profile_id and target_id nullable, backend_kind and dispatch_time nullable. Rule scope references exact profile/target IDs, Android user and display; global-input authority is a separate explicit scope. |
640	
641	
642	
643	Index target_app_profiles(connection_profile_id, enabled) and executions(connection_profile_id, admitted_at). Enable/disable, target identity and backend-scope mutations increment policy_revision and invalidate bound approvals. Endpoints and observed connection health are dynamic capability data, not grants. Credentials for outgoing ADB/runtime authentication must be reversibly encrypted; incoming MCP bearer credentials remain nonreversible verifiers.
644	
645	
646	## External host forwarding
647	
648	For host-to-phone connections use adb forward, not adb reverse. Select an explicit authorized serial and allocate a free host port; record ownership of the mapping and remove only that mapping on stop. Create separate mappings for MCP HTTPS and an optional target-runtime endpoint. [S19]
649	
650	```
651	adb -s SERIAL forward --no-rebind tcp:0 tcp:MCP_DEVICE_PORT
652	# Capture the allocated host port for the MCP client.
653	adb -s SERIAL forward --no-rebind tcp:0 tcp:RUNTIME_DEVICE_PORT
654	# Optional separately authorized runtime debug connection.
655	adb -s SERIAL forward --remove tcp:OWNED_HOST_PORT
656	```
657	
658	Both phone listeners and host forwards remain loopback-only. Do not use adb -a, expose port 5037, enable tcpip 5555, bind 0.0.0.0 or create an Internet tunnel. Verify actual listening addresses on the selected platform-tools build. ADB transport does not replace MCP authentication or paired HTTPS server verification; forwarded port changes must work with the client’s trust profile without disabling certificate validation.
659	
660	The host machine may itself be remotely operated through a separately secured environment, but ADB forwarding alone does not create Internet remote access. Host access and ADB authorization are powerful trust decisions outside ordinary MCP client scopes; a hostile independently authorized ADB host is not constrained by this bridge’s policy engine.
661	
662	
663	# 16 On demand screen state and coordinate taps
664	
665	The arbitrary-app convenience group provides screen.state and input.tap through a bounded portable manifest or opt-in dynamic aliases; these are not additional default bootstrap tools. The complete inventory remains separately searchable. It has no app-specific decision logic, automatic polling scheduler, offer handling or autonomous multi-step workflow. An agent supplies timing and interpretation. Existing settings, files and sensors remain reusable native capabilities; optional hierarchy is separate from pixel capture.
666	
667	| Tool | Contract and authorization boundary |
668	| --- | --- |
669	| screen.state | Input: connectionProfileId, displayId. Return a bounded PNG image plus width, height, displayId, rotation, captureId and capturedAt; identify the coordinate-space version. Capture only the currently rendered display, not hidden app state. Require an explicit screen-read scope; secure surfaces can be blank/blocked. No persisted screenshot logs. [S21] |
670	| input.tap | Input: x, y, displayId and optional referenceCaptureId, with an approved connection profile. Coordinates are integer physical display pixels in the published coordinate space. Reject out-of-bounds or unsupported displays. Require explicit device-wide input scope; Deny/Ask/Allow is configurable per client. |
671	| Optional context | Hierarchy and foreground/window context require separately enabled capabilities. Return their own timestamps and availability/error status; they are not an atomic snapshot with the screenshot. Missing hierarchy does not fabricate app semantics. |
672	
673	
674	
675	
676	## Coordinate and freshness contract
677	
678	A screen.state image is returned at its stated pixel dimensions; if an implementation scales or crops it, it must expose an explicit image-to-display transform and coordinateSpaceVersion. The client must map preview coordinates before input.tap. Never infer coordinates from CSS sizing, density-independent pixels or an unspecified screenshot scale.
679	
680	When referenceCaptureId is provided, require an unexpired capture belonging to this client, connection and display, and unchanged rotation, dimensions and coordinate-space version. Reject stale or mismatched references rather than remapping silently. Set a configurable short maximum age. A reference proves which coordinate frame was used, not that app content has stayed unchanged.
681	
682	Without a reference, direct-coordinate mode intentionally targets the current display geometry. Validate bounds and capability immediately before dispatch; record that no freshness reference was used. The client may receive Allow for on-demand taps without a new prompt every time. Ask prompts only when configured, and an approval never overrides stale coordinates or scope limits.
683	
684	
685	## Dispatch and outcome
686	
687	Translate into a fixed reviewed ADB operation with validated numeric arguments, bounded duration and no caller-supplied shell text. Host-side argument arrays alone do not solve device shell parsing. Return dispatched/completed/failed or outcome unknown with the call ID. A successful injection does not prove any particular app action occurred; the agent may request another screen.state. Do not retry a tap automatically after timeout or disconnect.
688	
689	Android input is display-wide, not package-addressed. Package or foreground checks may be optional best-effort guards, never a hard target-app boundary: focus can change between check and injection. Capture likewise sees the rendered screen, not two hidden app UIs at once. Shell authority is not root; private files, nondebuggable debugger access and secure-window bypass are not provided. [S22–S24]
690	
691	No app-specific workflow or polling scheduler is included. Additional operations exposed by the full binding inventory use their generated/generic contracts and client grants, not newly invented convenience workflows.
692	
693	
694	# 17 Internal Kotlin ARC engine and compatible external targets
695	
696	Port the ARC protocol/runtime behavior internally to Kotlin as specified in the detailed port contract below. The Compose target adapter and controller session UI use the same authorized services as MCP. Generic phone/app control remains the separate owner-paired ADB backend. Keep the retained arc-protobuf-v1 framing, protobuf tags and version1.0; do not embed a managed Avalonia server in the bridge. Protected local owner grants/approvals are excluded from every remote tree/frame/input path. The original external-only integration proposal is superseded; compatible external ARC targets remain supported by the planned Kotlin client adapter.

698	# 18 Protected consent and integration acceptance

Persisted Android URI grants belong to the bridge app; resource_grants is the narrower per client mapping. Recheck the actual OS grant and exact document identity on each use. ## Indexes and connection policy

Index credentials(client_id, state), client_tool_rules(tool_id), executions(client_id, admitted_at), audit_events(client_id, occurred_at), audit_events(occurred_at) and change_outbox(delivered_at, change_id). Add a partial unique index on executions(client_id, tool_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL. Generate keys per intended operation, not per HTTP retry; reject reuse with a different request digest.

Enable PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON for every connection and verify it. Use WAL on app private local storage, a bounded busy timeout, short transactions and a single application writer queue. Readers use short snapshots so they do not pin the WAL indefinitely. Start with synchronous=FULL for security relevant mutations; benchmark before changing durability. Schedule bounded checkpoints and monitor database, WAL and free disk sizes. [S8, S9]


## Permission commit and execution admission

```
with admissionGate:
  BEGIN IMMEDIATE
  assert client.row_version == expectedClientVersion
  assert policy_state.policy_revision == expectedPolicyRevision
  validate entire proposed rule set
  write rules; increment client.row_version and policy_revision
  append audit_event and change_outbox
  COMMIT
  install new immutable snapshot; invalidate old approvals
  signal affected calls and streams
// Acknowledge Apply only after the gate has published the commit
```

Execution admission uses the same gate: reevaluate the current snapshot, reserve/consume an in memory one use approval, insert the admitted execution and commit before dispatch. On persistence failure no call is issued; a reserved approval is invalidated rather than restored optimistically. Crash after commit but before or during Binder execution yields unknown, not automatic retry. SQLite cannot atomically commit a remote Android side effect.


# Secret protection and storage recovery


## Secrets and privacy

For token format credential_id.secret, look up the nonsecret ID and compare a constant time HMAC-SHA-256 verifier of the full token with a nonexportable Android Keystore key. SQLite stores the verifier and key alias, never the token or HMAC key. Separate keys protect transport server identity and any encrypted metadata. Hardware backing is checked, not assumed; Keystore protects extraction but a compromised app process may still invoke its keys. [S10]

Do not store caller secrets in SQLite connection strings, preferences, logs, analytics or crash attachments. Sensitive scope labels and identifiers may require application level encryption under a Keystore wrapped key, depending on threat model. Base SQLite is not encrypted by default. An encrypted provider is an additional dependency and deployment gate, not an implicit property of SQLite.


## Migrations and backup

Pause the listener for migrations, check schema/version and available space, apply each transactional migration and record its checksum only on success. Run foreign key and integrity checks. If a migration fails or the schema is newer than supported, remain stopped with a recovery message; do not reset the database or weaken policy. Use SQLite backup APIs or a tested consistent export, never copy only the live .db while WAL is active. [S11]

Exclude secrets, the live database and sidecars, approvals and sessions from both cloud backup and device transfer. Validate Android extraction rules on supported devices; allowBackup=false alone is not a universal device transfer guarantee. [S14] Export a versioned, integrity checked configuration package with scope review; encrypt exports containing private identifiers. Restore into a staging database, validate, preview changes, then activate atomically with all clients disabled, fresh revisions and fresh pairing. Keystore keys are not assumed portable.

# Tool exchanges and result behavior


## Settings and sensor semantics

Brightness write uses the documented raw 1 to 255 range, with a narrower default policy range such as 16 to 240. Check manual mode before dispatch and read back afterward; Settings.System does not provide an atomic compare and set across external actors. Do not change automatic mode or undo another actor’s change. Report a conflict or uncertain outcome honestly. Sensor rates are requested ceilings, not promised delivery timing; bound sample count and bytes, report actual timestamps, and always unregister listeners. [S15, S16]


## Example MCP exchange

```
POST /mcp
Authorization: Bearer <credential_id.secret>
MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-11-25
Mcp-Session-Id: <required-initialized-owned-session>
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json, text/event-stream

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":42,"method":"tools/call",
 "params":{"name":"contacts.list","arguments":{
   "contactIds":["contact_7"],
   "fields":["displayName"],"limit":1}}}

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":42,"result":{
 "content":[{"type":"text","text":"1 contact returned"}],
 "structuredContent":{"contacts":[{
   "id":"contact_7","displayName":"Example person"}]},
 "isError":false}}
```

This example assumes initialization, pairing, OS grant, scoped permission and any Ask approval already succeeded. The displayed contact is fictitious. Discovery advertises the matching output schema; the adapter validates and minimizes output before serialization. Cursors are opaque, client bound and invalidated by policy changes; they do not bypass field or row scope.


## Error contract and retries

Use protocol errors for malformed or unsupported JSON-RPC/MCP requests; use a tool result with isError for a valid call that cannot execute, with stable sanitized codes such as POLICY_DENIED, APPROVAL_EXPIRED, OS_PERMISSION_REQUIRED, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED or OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. Authentication failures stay at HTTP. Never return stack traces, Binder parcels or existence details to unauthorized callers. Read retries may be safe; write retries require adapter supported idempotency or explicit user review.


# 13 Threat model and operational limits

Protect user data, Android capabilities, approval integrity, credentials and policy history against malicious local apps, prompt injected agents, hostile websites reaching loopback, stolen client credentials and buggy target services. Device root or full bridge process compromise is outside the default trust guarantee; document this residual risk rather than implying Keystore or SQLite prevents it.

| Threat | Required mitigation and residual limit |
| --- | --- |
| Confused deputy | Resolve client identity before dispatch; authorize exact tool, resource and output. Native services see the bridge UID; ADB uses shell authority, not the original MCP principal. |
| Local port impersonation | Pin paired server identity with HTTPS where supported. Do not claim random ports or localhost authenticate the bridge. Plain HTTP mode is reduced assurance. |
| DNS rebinding or browser attack | Loopback only binding, Host and Origin validation, no permissive CORS, no cookie auth, per request bearer verification. No browser page can pair silently. |
| Prompt injection or consent spoofing | Agent text cannot grant policy. Local UI renders escaped text, bounded previews and trusted action labels; approval is bound to an immutable canonical plan. |
| Credential theft or replay | High entropy secrets, Keystore backed verifier, short setup window, redaction, rotation and immediate revocation. Bearer possession remains impersonation until revoked. |
| Scope escape | Resolve exact resources, schema hashes and owned handles. Generic and raw Binder calls use the same per-client gate, bounded marshalling and service identity checks; no unvalidated pointer or SQL pass-through. |
| Revocation race | Serialized admission boundary, revision recheck, invalidated approvals, canceled streams and no stale replay. Cannot undo a previously dispatched external effect. |
| Memory or Binder denial of service | Bound request sizes, nested JSON, concurrent calls, pending approvals, output and event buffers. Use deadlines and bounded worker pools, not UI or Binder thread blocking. |
| Backup or diagnostic leakage | Private app storage, protected exports, no secrets or raw-payload logging, disabled clients after restore and opt in redacted diagnostics. |
| Database tampering or downgrade | Constrained schema, integrity checks, version checks and fail closed restore. App sandbox is the baseline; full OS compromise is not solved by these checks. |




## Logging and data retention

Log opaque execution and client IDs, tool name, decision category, reason code, policy revision, latency and sanitized outcome. Never log Authorization headers, pairing secrets, full arguments, content URIs, contact names, document contents, raw Binder exceptions or SSE payloads. A request digest may itself enable correlation; retain only when needed, preferably keyed, and do not treat it as anonymous data.

Optional call logging follows Section 14, with Off, Metadata and expiring Redacted diagnostic modes. Suggested mandatory audit default: 7 days of local redacted audit metadata and a fixed storage cap with owner controlled deletion. Configuration change audit should be durable; if it cannot be recorded, reject that mutation. For tool dispatch, failure to record admission fails closed. Logging is not tamper proof against full app compromise. Metrics and support exports are opt in and previewed before sharing.


# 14 Configurable call logging per client

The local owner configures optional call logging independently for every authenticated client. Off means no optional call records, not zero security records: the minimal permission, revocation and execution-admission audit remains mandatory. A remote client cannot enable its own diagnostics, change retention or export logs.

| Mode | Captured data and limits |
| --- | --- |
| Off | No optional call records. Mandatory minimal security/admission audit still applies. |
| Metadata default | Server-generated call ID, client ID, tool/backend ID, timestamps, duration, bounded decision/outcome code and revision numbers. No headers, targets, argument values or free-text errors. |
| Redacted diagnostic | Explicit per-client, time-limited opt-in. Add only adapter-defined, schema-validated derived fields such as counts, enum state and rounded timings. Redact before buffering. Never raw arguments, full results, screenshots, UI text, credentials, shell text or Binder parcels. |




## Logging tab and owner controls

Clients > selected client > Logging shows mode, diagnostic expiry, retention, storage used/cap, per-record cap and dropped-record count. Proposed defaults: Metadata, 7-day retention, 10 MiB per client, 100 MiB total and a 4 KiB maximum diagnostic projection; a diagnostic session expires after 15 minutes. These are tunable design defaults, always bounded by global limits. Show a preview of the exact fields each tool may record before enabling diagnostics.

Apply uses expected logging_revision, with the same draft/review/conflict experience as permissions. Pause stops future optional capture without deleting history. Purge optional logs deletes this client’s optional records and queued projections, not the security audit. Export is an explicit local-owner action over a bounded, redacted snapshot; warn that exported copies are outside later expiry or purge enforcement. RemoteControl and ADB input must not trigger these controls.

Diagnostic expires on restart. |

Keep a reserved, bounded budget for required security audit. Do not let a diagnostic flood consume all device storage.


# Logging lifecycle and failure semantics

Keep logging_revision separate from authorization policy_revision. Ordinary logging changes do not broaden tool authority or invalidate otherwise unchanged Ask approvals. At request admission, capture the permitted logging ceiling; before every optional emission and commit, intersect that ceiling with current client settings and current global limits.

```
effectiveCapture = admissionLoggingCeiling
                   INTERSECT currentClientLoggingConfig
                   INTERSECT currentGlobalLimits
// Enabling more capture affects new calls only.
// Reductions, expiry and revocation affect queued writes immediately.
```

Enabling diagnostics during a call never reconstructs prior inputs or expands that call’s captured fields. Pausing, lowering the level, diagnostic expiry or client revocation suppresses further optional capture and discards now-disallowed buffers. Serialize queued writes against logging reductions so a stale snapshot cannot commit afterward. Shorter retention also reduces expiry of existing records; longer retention does not silently extend their original expiry.


## Security and data handling

- Encrypt diagnostic projections with keys protected by Android Keystore. Use an independently destroyable per-client log-domain key if cryptographic deletion is required. Never reuse the mandatory-audit key for optional-log deletion. Plain SQLite is not encryption.

- Adapter-defined allowlists are primary; regex redaction is only a secondary defense. Credentials, authorization headers, pairing codes, ADB private keys, target runtime tokens, clipboard/text input, UI text, file contents and screen images are always excluded, even when diagnostics are enabled.

- Known authenticated denied calls may be attributed to that client and logged according to its settings, without denied argument values. Unauthenticated attempts have no trustworthy client ownership: use a separate rate-limited security aggregate, never an attacker-supplied client ID.

- Log admitted, dispatched, completed, failed, canceled and outcome unknown distinctly. Admission does not prove a side effect happened. executions.state already includes dispatched; extend its diagnostic metadata and record dispatch time when observable; process death can still make the true outcome unknown.


## Failure and deletion behavior

Optional logger failures drop bounded optional records and increment aggregate counters; they neither permit a denied action nor block an already authorized action merely to preserve diagnostics. Required pre-dispatch admission-audit failure remains fail closed for all execution admissions. A completion-audit failure after an irreversible effect cannot undo that effect: report the audit gap/unknown status and never reexecute solely to obtain a log.

Purge must clear queued projections, committed rows, indexes/caches and prepared local exports. Ordinary SQLite deletion does not guarantee immediate physical erasure from WAL files, backups or flash storage. Checkpoint/vacuum policies and independently destroyable encryption keys address different risks; do not promise secure erasure without evidence.


## Logging acceptance checks

Test client isolation; Off-to-diagnostic during a call; diagnostic-to-Off/expiry/revocation racing a queued write; secret canaries; per-client/global quota pressure; retention shortening; export review; purge versus mandatory audit; disk-full drop counting; and post-effect audit failure without duplicate execution.


# 15 Authorized ADB execution architecture

The primary arbitrary-app control path is App A agent -> authenticated MCP bridge -> typed ADB adapter -> owner-paired adbd -> the visible UI of App B. App B does not need Avalonia or embedded instrumentation for on-demand screen.state and input.tap operations. Optional UI hierarchy is a separately permissioned capability, not a prerequisite. This is reusable visible-UI access, not private-data access or full debugging of every application.


## Three distinct backend modes

| Mode | Connection and trust |
| --- | --- |
| Self ADB primary | An embedded/native ADB client connects from the bridge app to this device’s owner-enabled Wireless Debugging service. Android 11+ is the starting compatibility target, subject to device support. Owner explicitly enables and pairs it. LADB demonstrates feasibility, not a selected dependency or license approval. [S17, S18] |
| External ADB host | An already-authorized USB or securely paired wireless host forwards its localhost socket to a phone loopback endpoint. Keep the host ADB server and forwards local. This is separate from the same-device ADB client profile. [S19] |
| Avalonia runtime optional | A target app embeds an opted-in Avalonia.RemoteControl runtime. A new Android protocol adapter controls only its exposed Avalonia root. This specialized route is not required for arbitrary-app ADB automation. [S20] |



MCP client identity, ADB paired-host identity and target-app identity are different principals. A paired ADB key establishes backend access, not a per-agent permission grant. Every MCP call still passes the bridge policy engine. Ordinary adbd commands use shell authority, not root and not the bridge UID. Device policy, user/profile boundaries, protected windows and platform restrictions remain upper bounds.


## Pairing and lifecycle

1. In local Settings > Connections, create a Self ADB profile. Explain the broad shell authority and require the owner to enable Wireless Debugging and confirm its pairing code in Android settings. Never enable debugging, accept a pairing prompt or change security settings silently.

1. Use the pairing endpoint only for pairing, then discover the authenticated connect endpoint. Ports may differ and change after reboot, debugging toggle or network changes. Track Unpaired, Paired offline, Connecting, Connected, Locked and Revoked separately.

1. Persist the ADB key encrypted under a Keystore-protected wrapping key and exclude it from backup/export/logs. A native ADB implementation may need plaintext key material in process; do not claim the ADB private key is nonexportable or hardware backed unless proven.

1. On disconnect, stop admissions that need ADB, cancel bounded collectors and mark dispatched unknown outcomes honestly. Reconnect with the same trusted profile only after endpoint rediscovery and peer verification; never fall back to unauthenticated tcpip 5555.

Owner Disconnect pauses this connection. Revoke deletes local key material and requires Android-side revocation/forgetting of the paired identity to remove device trust fully. A stored local status must not claim the Android pairing was revoked without confirmation. Device reboot or force-stop recovery is best effort, not an always-on guarantee.

## External host forwarding

For host-to-phone connections use adb forward, not adb reverse. Select an explicit authorized serial and allocate a free host port; record ownership of the mapping and remove only that mapping on stop. Create separate mappings for MCP HTTPS and an optional target-runtime endpoint. [S19]

```
adb -s SERIAL forward --no-rebind tcp:0 tcp:MCP_DEVICE_PORT
# Capture the allocated host port for the MCP client.
adb -s SERIAL forward --no-rebind tcp:0 tcp:RUNTIME_DEVICE_PORT
# Optional separately authorized runtime debug connection.
adb -s SERIAL forward --remove tcp:OWNED_HOST_PORT
```

Both phone listeners and host forwards remain loopback-only. Do not use adb -a, expose port 5037, enable tcpip 5555, bind 0.0.0.0 or create an Internet tunnel. Verify actual listening addresses on the selected platform-tools build. ADB transport does not replace MCP authentication or paired HTTPS server verification; forwarded port changes must work with the client’s trust profile without disabling certificate validation.

The host machine may itself be remotely operated through a separately secured environment, but ADB forwarding alone does not create Internet remote access. Host access and ADB authorization are powerful trust decisions outside ordinary MCP client scopes; a hostile independently authorized ADB host is not constrained by this bridge’s policy engine.


# 16 On demand screen state and coordinate taps

The arbitrary-app convenience group provides screen.state and input.tap through a bounded portable manifest or opt-in dynamic aliases; these are not additional default bootstrap tools. The complete inventory remains separately searchable. It has no app-specific decision logic, automatic polling scheduler, offer handling or autonomous multi-step workflow. An agent supplies timing and interpretation. Existing settings, files and sensors remain reusable native capabilities; optional hierarchy is separate from pixel capture.

| Tool | Contract and authorization boundary |
| --- | --- |
| screen.state | Input: connectionProfileId, displayId. Return a bounded PNG image plus width, height, displayId, rotation, captureId and capturedAt; identify the coordinate-space version. Capture only the currently rendered display, not hidden app state. Require an explicit screen-read scope; secure surfaces can be blank/blocked. No persisted screenshot logs. [S21] |
| input.tap | Input: x, y, displayId and optional referenceCaptureId, with an approved connection profile. Coordinates are integer physical display pixels in the published coordinate space. Reject out-of-bounds or unsupported displays. Require explicit device-wide input scope; Deny/Ask/Allow is configurable per client. |
| Optional context | Hierarchy and foreground/window context require separately enabled capabilities. Return their own timestamps and availability/error status; they are not an atomic snapshot with the screenshot. Missing hierarchy does not fabricate app semantics. |




## Coordinate and freshness contract

A screen.state image is returned at its stated pixel dimensions; if an implementation scales or crops it, it must expose an explicit image-to-display transform and coordinateSpaceVersion. The client must map preview coordinates before input.tap. Never infer coordinates from CSS sizing, density-independent pixels or an unspecified screenshot scale.

When referenceCaptureId is provided, require an unexpired capture belonging to this client, connection and display, and unchanged rotation, dimensions and coordinate-space version. Reject stale or mismatched references rather than remapping silently. Set a configurable short maximum age. A reference proves which coordinate frame was used, not that app content has stayed unchanged.

Without a reference, direct-coordinate mode intentionally targets the current display geometry. Validate bounds and capability immediately before dispatch; record that no freshness reference was used. The client may receive Allow for on-demand taps without a new prompt every time. Ask prompts only when configured, and an approval never overrides stale coordinates or scope limits.


## Dispatch and outcome

Translate into a fixed reviewed ADB operation with validated numeric arguments, bounded duration and no caller-supplied shell text. Host-side argument arrays alone do not solve device shell parsing. Return dispatched/completed/failed or outcome unknown with the call ID. A successful injection does not prove any particular app action occurred; the agent may request another screen.state. Do not retry a tap automatically after timeout or disconnect.

Android input is display-wide, not package-addressed. Package or foreground checks may be optional best-effort guards, never a hard target-app boundary: focus can change between check and injection. Capture likewise sees the rendered screen, not two hidden app UIs at once. Shell authority is not root; private files, nondebuggable debugger access and secure-window bypass are not provided. [S22–S24]

No app-specific workflow or polling scheduler is included. Additional operations exposed by the full binding inventory use their generated/generic contracts and client grants, not newly invented convenience workflows.
