1115	### Exact framing and dispatch profile
1116	
1117	Each frame is a four-byte signed32-bit big-endian payload length followed by precisely that many protobuf bytes. The inspected default maximum payload is8MiB. Reject negative lengths, configured maxima below1, oversized lengths and truncated prefix/payload before allocating unbounded memory. A zero-length protobuf payload is syntactically permitted by the codec but yields an empty envelope that fails protocol validation; it is not an authenticated request. A streaming decoder must retain partial prefix/payload and consume exactly one frame at a time without losing coalesced bytes. The complete-frame decoder rejects extra/trailing bytes; the stream reader treats them as the next frame. These are different APIs, not inconsistent acceptance rules.
1118	
1119	BridgeRequest fields are protocol_version1:string, request_id2:string, method3:BridgeMethod, authorization4:string and payload5:bytes. BridgeResponse fields are protocol_version1:string, request_id2:string, status3:BridgeStatus, payload4:bytes, error_message5:string and end_of_stream6:bool. Authentication uses the request-envelope Bearer value, not HTTP headers on a TCP socket. Response request ID and version must match. Unknown protobuf fields are preserved by the chosen generated model on decode/re-encode; unknown enum values remain representable and unsupported methods fail without dispatch. Descriptors must not reinterpret unknown values as method0 or OK.

1141	### Transport, authorization and owner-control isolation
1142	
1143	The inspected RemoteControlBridgeTcpListener uses loopback TCP NetworkStream without a TLS handshake. IsAdbTunnel is a configuration assertion, not encryption or proof that a socket was forwarded. Kotlin ArcTcpTransport therefore implements the same authenticated loopback plaintext ARC profile explicitly and is disabled until locally enabled. It does not label that profile TLS. The MCP HTTPS listener remains separate. A future authenticated secure tunnel can carry unchanged ARC bytes, but its negotiation, certificate/peer verification and client compatibility must be explicit. Do not expose plaintext ARC on a network interface or enable an unverified tunnel flag to bypass policy.
1144	
1145	Marker schemaVersion="1", devicePort, token and bridgeProtocol retain their upstream discovery meanings. A marker is app-private, created only after successful bind and removed on stop. No secret token is placed in logs, public catalog or design examples. Debuggable run-as discovery and owner-authorized ADB forwarding are not promised for every release package. Kotlin clients reject an unknown marker protocol; missing protocol is handled only by the documented legacy gRPC selection policy, never guessed as ARC. Session state is local per connection/authenticated principal and credential/target epoch; ARCv1 has no new session token, replay cursor, multiplexing or TLS field. The supplied token maps to an independently configured ARC principal and exact target scope; it is not an MCP session ID, Android permission or local-owner approval.
1146	
1147	The Kotlin ArcAuthorizationGate delegates all operation admission to the canonical bridge policy and checks target capability before the handler. Capabilities may be reduced by policy; mutation/frame/input flags never advertise an implemented capability that is absent. Recheck credential/policy/target epochs during long streams, terminate on revocation, and suppress protected content before capture/serialization. All ARC paths (including direct client input) share this gate with MCP-created ARC plans. The local Compose management approval flow is never exported as an ARC root. Entering protected pairing/grant/export/Ask screens quiesces ARC/ADB input and stream exposure, invalidates queued gestures and requires fresh owner authentication for the exact command. Arbitrary local apps cannot bind the unexported service or use a plain ARC token to approve grants.

1230	## Callback object construction and reachability
1231	
1232	CallbackDescriptor.materialization_strategy has closed values interface_dynamic_proxy, binder_generic_stub, prebuilt_adapter and unsupported_abstract_class. A public Java interface can use java.lang.reflect.Proxy with the exact source-proven interface list, declared methods and supported classloader. An AIDL callback uses a reviewed generic android.os.Binder subclass: attach/query the pinned descriptor, implement onTransact using the exact verified transaction IDs, flags and codecs, enforce interface tokens and sender UID/capability before handing off to the broker. Parcel/file-descriptor/Binder-handle lifetimes are bounded and released on every failure. This is not a universal AIDL compiler, non-SDK access bypass or arbitrary Binder-handle import.
1233	
1234	An abstract callback class cannot use java.lang.reflect.Proxy. It is registration-unsupported with ABSTRACT_CLASS_NO_RUNTIME_SUBCLASS unless a reviewed prebuilt Kotlin/Java subclass adapter is shipped and its adapter ID/version/hash and supported callback methods are pinned. No runtime dex/bytecode generation or downloaded executable code is selected. The catalog still identifies every abstract callback and its unknown/unreachable variants. SDK/Java invocation resolves public members at admission through java.lang.reflect or supported MethodHandles from the exact pinned JVM signature; do not ship hundreds of thousands of per-member wrappers. R8 keep rules preserve only reviewed bridge adapters and reflective entry points. Non-SDK/access failures are explicit NON_SDK_BLOCKED/OS_UNAVAILABLE reasons, never silently retried through a stronger identity.
1235	
1236	Permitted Binder-handle acquisition is (a) public bindService to an explicit exported component with package/signing identity verification, or (b) a handle returned by a documented public SDK handle-source method. Platform ServiceManager lookup and manager-private proxy fields are non-SDK; the ordinary app backend reports backend_unreachable:non_sdk instead of promising access. A separate ADB raw adapter may expose only reviewed fixed service-call operations supported by shell authority and its actual marshalling limits. That is not an app-UID IBinder handle, a generic verified Parcelable codec or permission to use hwbinder. Raw connection_id is either a real connection_profiles.profile_id or reserved platform:local; object handles pin that profile, user, target and backend epoch and cannot migrate between them. HIDL declarations and completion semantics remain inventory/classification. No ordinary app backend is assumed to access hwbinder; unsupported paths report backend_unreachable:hidl. A future separately reviewed privileged backend would require an explicit scope/design change, not an inferred owner grant.

1238	## Startup reuse and bounded admission
1239	
1240	A new boot invalidates old admission capabilities, process-local object handles and approvals. It does not require discarding a validated semantic selection cache. Reuse is allowed only if a fresh supported capability observation matches the cache's canonical semantic facts (platform/minor/extensions/build/OEM/module/interface identity and relevant availability), scope, inventory root, catalog/overlay generations, resolver/schema version and type-graph digest. Boot ID, observation time and transient handle IDs are excluded from that semantic key, but remain new runtime evidence. Verify the app-private cache seal against the Keystore-authenticated manifest, open the immutable generation and create a new view revision bound to the new boot/capability epoch; do not mutate/relabel the old view. File identity/generation and on-read page/document hashes detect stale/corrupt data; failure quarantines the cache and closes device admission. Root/full process compromise remains outside the stated trust guarantee. Every runtime permission/reachability/wire/handle check is fresh at dispatch regardless of cache reuse.
1241	
1242	For the API level35 (Android15) or later, 8GiB/128GB reference profile and approximately800k-entry inventory, proposed unmeasured p95 acceptance targets are <=600seconds for cold complete indexed resolution and <=10seconds for warm validated semantic reuse. Resolve in bounded batches, SQLite staging and indexed reverse-type worklists: application scratch<=64MiB, SQLite page cache<=64MiB, total service peak<=384MiB and disk scratch<=incoming catalog size. A large dependency closure that exceeds a bound spills to validated SQLite worklists or fails explicitly; it is not silently cut. Recompute affected closures on capability change, and perform full cold rebuild when compatibility keys or dependency provenance are insufficient. While Resolving, only authenticated policy/status, callback.status/callback.cancel and bindings.search/list/get are admitted; discovery reports resolving applicability. Device-affecting calls return VIEW_RESOLVING. Progress and cancellation remain bounded; the listener may be ready while device admission is unavailable, with separate status fields. These targets need real Android benchmarks; the historical Python4.30GiB/565.6second probe does not satisfy them.

1244	## Catalog delivery and management API ownership
1245

BridgeService obtains the owner-granted read capability, preflights capacity, streams bounded copy chunks into a new app-private staging file, hashes the exact copied bytes and fsyncs before matching the independently trusted manifest size/SHA. ## Kotlin server and Jetpack Compose management UI

The user's latest language decisions supersede the original Avalonia12/.NET management-stack requirement: both the MCP server and management UI are Kotlin. Ship one Android APK, one application UID and initially one application process. A Kotlin started foreground BridgeService owns the server and all authoritative state; a Kotlin ComponentActivity hosts Jetpack Compose presentation. The activity binds to the already-started service through an unexported local Binder facade, never through an unauthenticated loopback admin endpoint. This same-process facade is not a new privilege boundary. There is no managed runtime, C# server, .NET UI or Kestrel requirement. Python extraction and offline reference models remain build/validation tooling, not delivered Kotlin server implementation.

BridgeService owns MCP initialization/transport/authentication, persistent listener and notification lifecycle, client policy/approval admission, catalog and SQLite transactions, version/type resolution, Binder/ADB adapters, callback journal/cleanup and functional discovery/activation. Only its repositories open the writable configuration database; the activity submits typed commands with expected revisions and observes immutable state. SQLite platform APIs and prepared statements provide the executable-DDL path; any alternative persistence layer must pass the same constraints, migrations and transactions. Do not assume an ORM automatically preserves trigger behavior. Catalog snapshots are read-only handles after validation; replacement uses the established staging/activation protocol.

The local facade exposes bounded operations for status, paginated catalog/group/subscription reads and authorized owner commands. It accepts no arbitrary SQL, reflection, raw object graph or universal service reference. The Compose ViewModel uses lifecycle-aware asynchronous state collection, and long work runs in service-owned coroutine scopes on bounded IO/worker executors. Activity destruction cancels observers and pending presentation work, not accepted server operations or the foreground service. Client disconnect/BindService disconnect yields reconnecting/stale UI state, not a false Running indication. The app does not equate possession of an in-process UI reference with authorization: owner-sensitive commands require the existing fresh authenticated owner approval bound to nonce, exact operation, expected revisions and expiry. Remote tool calls cannot submit that local approval capability. Same UID and same process are not evidence of physical touch or user intent; the remote-input quiescence and owner-authentication gates still apply.

Startup validates config migration, desired-state and keystore availability, obtains an eligible foreground-service start, begins its foreground notification within platform deadlines, loads trusted catalog/capability snapshots and admits only a ready device view. Listener bind/initialization determines Running. A bound activity alone does not start or preserve server readiness. Stop persists desired state first, closes admission, suppresses callback delivery, performs bounded recorded cleanup, closes transports/journals/storage and reports any uncertain remote outcomes before stopSelf; it cannot wait indefinitely for a device. Activity and notification Stop actions enter the same service command path. The service owns notification updates; the Compose AppBar renders the same state stream with separate MCP and ADB health. Optional boot/restart remains subject to all previously documented Android restrictions.

The Compose UI preserves client pairing, grants, logging controls, catalog CRUD/overrides/history, full inventory and permission fields, device availability, functional-group editor/job search, loaded-session budgets, subscriptions and cancellation, protected approvals, connection profiles and status. Config CAS commits atomically update storage, policy/cache epochs and a transactional outbox; the service publishes state and standard MCP change hints only after commit. Simultaneous activity and MCP catalog edits either commit against the expected revision or conflict, never silently overwrite. Pending owner approvals bind the exact server plan and are invalidated by relevant revision/identity changes. UI-side validation is a convenience; the server repeats authoritative validation.

Generic phone/app control remains the authorized ADB screen.state/input.tap path, independent of Compose internals. The bridge's ordinary Kotlin UI can be inspected/controlled by that same permitted rendered-screen path, subject to protected-owner-surface restrictions; a Compose semantics/test API is not exposed as a production remote-control bypass. SharpNinja.Avalonia.RemoteControl remains only an optional protocol-compatible external-target adapter for apps that deliberately embed its Android Runtime/Protocol. It is not a bridge UI dependency and requires no .NET runtime inside the Kotlin bridge. A Kotlin adapter would implement the pinned framing/protobuf protocol and target-authentication contract directly; if no verified implementation is present, report adapter_unsupported rather than imply cross-runtime method calls.

## Internal Kotlin ARC compatibility port

The user explicitly requires porting Avalonia.RemoteControl internally to Kotlin while retaining ARC protocol compatibility. This supersedes the earlier external-adapter-only proposal. The Kotlin bridge includes a designed ArcEngine module and ComposeTargetAdapter; it does not depend on a managed Avalonia runtime. Existing compatible ARC clients remain the interoperability target. External Avalonia targets remain possible through the same pinned protocol client adapter. This task specifies the port and test contract; it does not claim the Kotlin port or Compose remote dispatcher is implemented.

### Pinned upstream and compatibility boundary

The inspected upstream is sharpninja/Avalonia.RemoteControl commit19792a52a13a3df342f90bab6b246b547e673919. The protocol and runtime/client source copies have individual SHA-256 hashes in the task's acquisition manifest. Protocol sources are [remote_control.proto](https://github.com/sharpninja/Avalonia.RemoteControl/blob/19792a52a13a3df342f90bab6b246b547e673919/src/Avalonia.RemoteControl.Protocol/Protos/remote_control.proto), [BridgeFrameCodec](https://github.com/sharpninja/Avalonia.RemoteControl/blob/19792a52a13a3df342f90bab6b246b547e673919/src/Avalonia.RemoteControl.Protocol/BridgeFrameCodec.cs), [request handler](https://github.com/sharpninja/Avalonia.RemoteControl/blob/19792a52a13a3df342f90bab6b246b547e673919/src/Avalonia.RemoteControl.Runtime/Bridge/RemoteControlBridgeRequestHandler.cs), [TCP listener](https://github.com/sharpninja/Avalonia.RemoteControl/blob/19792a52a13a3df342f90bab6b246b547e673919/src/Avalonia.RemoteControl.Runtime/Bridge/RemoteControlBridgeTcpListener.cs), and [official client](https://github.com/sharpninja/Avalonia.RemoteControl/blob/19792a52a13a3df342f90bab6b246b547e673919/src/Avalonia.RemoteControl.Client/Bridge/RemoteControlBridgeClient.cs). The portable design's arc-protocol-contract.json is a derived field/enum reference, not new protobuf definitions or an implemented port.

Retain marker bridgeProtocol=arc-protobuf-v1, protobuf package avalonia.remotecontrol.v1, protocol_version="1.0", all field numbers, scalar/repeated types, method/status enum numeric values and payload semantics. Do not rename the wire protocol to Kotlin, MCP or Compose. The gRPC service declaration shares payload messages but is not the Android ARC transport; implementing length-prefixed ARC does not imply a gRPC host. Kotlin package names may differ internally without changing protobuf descriptors. Generate the Kotlin/JVM-compatible protobuf model from the pinned schema in the implementation phase; any descriptor evolution is separately versioned/reviewed, not a silent field-number reuse.

### Exact framing and dispatch profile

Each frame is a four-byte signed32-bit big-endian payload length followed by precisely that many protobuf bytes. The inspected default maximum payload is8MiB. Reject negative lengths, configured maxima below1, oversized lengths and truncated prefix/payload before allocating unbounded memory. A zero-length protobuf payload is syntactically permitted by the codec but yields an empty envelope that fails protocol validation; it is not an authenticated request. A streaming decoder must retain partial prefix/payload and consume exactly one frame at a time without losing coalesced bytes. The complete-frame decoder rejects extra/trailing bytes; the stream reader treats them as the next frame. These are different APIs, not inconsistent acceptance rules.

BridgeRequest fields are protocol_version1:string, request_id2:string, method3:BridgeMethod, authorization4:string and payload5:bytes. BridgeResponse fields are protocol_version1:string, request_id2:string, status3:BridgeStatus, payload4:bytes, error_message5:string and end_of_stream6:bool. Authentication uses the request-envelope Bearer value, not HTTP headers on a TCP socket. Response request ID and version must match. Unknown protobuf fields are preserved by the chosen generated model on decode/re-encode; unknown enum values remain representable and unsupported methods fail without dispatch. Descriptors must not reinterpret unknown values as method0 or OK.

| BridgeMethod number | Payload / response | Inspected behavior to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 UNSPECIFIED | none | Unsupported. |
| 1 GET_CAPABILITIES | GetCapabilitiesRequest / GetCapabilitiesResponse | Authenticated unary; advertised flags reflect actual adapter support. |
| 2 GET_SNAPSHOT | GetSnapshotRequest / TreeSnapshot | Authenticated unary; typed current tree. |
| 3 WATCH_TREE | WatchTreeRequest / TreeUpdate | Repeated nonterminal response frames; terminal response closes stream. |
| 4 INVOKE_CLICK | InvokeClickRequest / CommandResult | Guarded target action; command failure distinct from transport failure. |
| 5 INVOKE_FOCUS | InvokeFocusRequest / CommandResult | Guarded focus action. |
| 6 SET_PROPERTY | SetPropertyRequest / CommandResult | Approved typed public property only; no arbitrary reflection. |
| 7 WATCH_LOGS | WatchLogsRequest / LogEntry | Filtered/redacted bounded logs with dropped_count. |
| 8 CANCEL | no dispatched payload in inspected handler | Reserved enum exists but handler has no Cancel case. Do not invent compatible remote-cancel RPC. |
| 9 WATCH_FRAMES | WatchFramesRequest / FrameUpdate | PNG frames with dimensions, root size, scale and timestamp. |
| 10 SEND_INPUT | SendInputRequest / CommandResult | Ordered input-event batch subject to policy and adapter support. |

BridgeStatus numbers remain0 UNSPECIFIED,1 OK,2 ERROR,3 UNAUTHENTICATED,4 UNAUTHORIZED,5 UNSUPPORTED,6 CANCELLED. A unary success/failure is end_of_stream=true; stream items usefalse, and a completed stream ends with a terminal response, possibly empty payload. The current listener reads one request per TCP connection; streaming is multiple responses for that request, not multiplexed requests. The official client cancels by cancellation/disposal of its socket. Method8 must return UNSUPPORTED in this compatibility profile. Closing ARC transport and cancelling an Android callback subscription are separate operations: the MCP callback broker retains its explicit lifecycle contract.

Tree and frame sequence fields are uint64, distinct from request IDs and callback-journal sequence/cursors. TreeNode preserves stable per-target IDs, parent IDs, type/name/automation identity, visible/enabled/focused flags, property metadata/classes and local/absolute bounds. Compose nodes expose truthful Compose semantics or a documented adapter identity, never pretend to be Avalonia Control objects. Properties unsupported by the Compose adapter remain unavailable/read-only with accurate capability/result; compatibility means the same wire/type meaning, not fabricated control-tree equivalence. Node IDs carry a target-generation boundary and stale IDs fail after root recreation.

Input retains enum values (pointer move1, press2, release3, wheel4, keydown5, keyup6, text7; mouse buttons unspecified0/left1/right2/middle3), root-relative DIP coordinates and event order. The Compose adapter converts DIP/root bounds and frame render_scale using the same captured root generation; it rejects nonfinite/out-of-root values, stale node/frame targets and unsupported key/property actions. Pointer/button/key state must be released on cancellation, root replacement, revocation and shutdown. It cannot claim universal Android input injection: generic phone input belongs to the separately authorized ADB backend. Frame streaming uses bounded PNG capture, preserves pixel/root dimensions and scale, redacts/excludes protected management surfaces and releases bitmap buffers. Upstream WatchFramesRequest.max_frames_per_second exists but the inspected handler parses and does not apply it; the port must not claim that field is an enforced upstream negotiated rate. Apply documented local server caps; any new guaranteed client rate semantics require a compatible reviewed profile.

### Transport, authorization and owner-control isolation

The inspected RemoteControlBridgeTcpListener uses loopback TCP NetworkStream without a TLS handshake. IsAdbTunnel is a configuration assertion, not encryption or proof that a socket was forwarded. Kotlin ArcTcpTransport therefore implements the same authenticated loopback plaintext ARC profile explicitly and is disabled until locally enabled. It does not label that profile TLS. The MCP HTTPS listener remains separate. A future authenticated secure tunnel can carry unchanged ARC bytes, but its negotiation, certificate/peer verification and client compatibility must be explicit. Do not expose plaintext ARC on a network interface or enable an unverified tunnel flag to bypass policy.

Marker schemaVersion="1", devicePort, token and bridgeProtocol retain their upstream discovery meanings. A marker is app-private, created only after successful bind and removed on stop. No secret token is placed in logs, public catalog or design examples. Debuggable run-as discovery and owner-authorized ADB forwarding are not promised for every release package. Kotlin clients reject an unknown marker protocol; missing protocol is handled only by the documented legacy gRPC selection policy, never guessed as ARC. Session state is local per connection/authenticated principal and credential/target epoch; ARCv1 has no new session token, replay cursor, multiplexing or TLS field. The supplied token maps to an independently configured ARC principal and exact target scope; it is not an MCP session ID, Android permission or local-owner approval.

The Kotlin ArcAuthorizationGate delegates all operation admission to the canonical bridge policy and checks target capability before the handler. Capabilities may be reduced by policy; mutation/frame/input flags never advertise an implemented capability that is absent. Recheck credential/policy/target epochs during long streams, terminate on revocation, and suppress protected content before capture/serialization. All ARC paths (including direct client input) share this gate with MCP-created ARC plans. The local Compose management approval flow is never exported as an ARC root. Entering protected pairing/grant/export/Ask screens quiesces ARC/ADB input and stream exposure, invalidates queued gestures and requires fresh owner authentication for the exact command. Arbitrary local apps cannot bind the unexported service or use a plain ARC token to approve grants.

### Port modules and class responsibilities

ArcProtocolModel preserves the pinned descriptor; ArcFrameCodec performs bounded incremental framing; ArcTcpTransport owns accepted sockets and cancellation; ArcCompatibilityProfile validates marker/version/status semantics; ArcAuthenticator resolves token to principal; ArcSessionRegistry owns per-connection epoch/state; ArcRequestHandler maps method IDs to typed ArcRuntime operations. ArcRuntime uses ArcAuthorizationGate, TargetAdapter, bounded stream buffers and AuditLogger. ComposeTargetAdapter implements tree/frame/action/input contracts using a protected, explicitly selected root through UiDispatcher; AdbPhoneBackend is a separate generic device adapter with different authority. ArcClientAdapter communicates with external compatible runtimes. None of these components impersonates an in-process Avalonia object or embeds a .NET server.

ComposeManagementViewModel uses the local OwnerCommandFacade for configuration, active roots, ARC status, client grants and logging. It is not the remote client and does not accept remote approval callbacks. Service shutdown stops ARC acceptance, terminates streams, releases pressed input state, removes markers and records unknown side-effect outcomes within a deadline. Bounded queue overflow terminates a frame/tree stream or reports the protocol-supported loss representation (logs have dropped_count); it never invents a new v1 wire field for unrepresented losses. Slow clients cannot block UI dispatch or allocate unbounded frame buffers.

## Verified design mechanisms after round013

These mechanisms are normative for this revision and replace conflicting earlier wording. They are design contracts, not Kotlin implementation claims. The finding ledger retains all28 original findings, including the brightness claim refuted by the current official source.

## Callback object construction and reachability

CallbackDescriptor.materialization_strategy has closed values interface_dynamic_proxy, binder_generic_stub, prebuilt_adapter and unsupported_abstract_class. A public Java interface can use java.lang.reflect.Proxy with the exact source-proven interface list, declared methods and supported classloader. An AIDL callback uses a reviewed generic android.os.Binder subclass: attach/query the pinned descriptor, implement onTransact using the exact verified transaction IDs, flags and codecs, enforce interface tokens and sender UID/capability before handing off to the broker. Parcel/file-descriptor/Binder-handle lifetimes are bounded and released on every failure. This is not a universal AIDL compiler, non-SDK access bypass or arbitrary Binder-handle import.

An abstract callback class cannot use java.lang.reflect.Proxy. It is registration-unsupported with ABSTRACT_CLASS_NO_RUNTIME_SUBCLASS unless a reviewed prebuilt Kotlin/Java subclass adapter is shipped and its adapter ID/version/hash and supported callback methods are pinned. No runtime dex/bytecode generation or downloaded executable code is selected. The catalog still identifies every abstract callback and its unknown/unreachable variants. SDK/Java invocation resolves public members at admission through java.lang.reflect or supported MethodHandles from the exact pinned JVM signature; do not ship hundreds of thousands of per-member wrappers. R8 keep rules preserve only reviewed bridge adapters and reflective entry points. Non-SDK/access failures are explicit NON_SDK_BLOCKED/OS_UNAVAILABLE reasons, never silently retried through a stronger identity.

Permitted Binder-handle acquisition is (a) public bindService to an explicit exported component with package/signing identity verification, or (b) a handle returned by a documented public SDK handle-source method. Platform ServiceManager lookup and manager-private proxy fields are non-SDK; the ordinary app backend reports backend_unreachable:non_sdk instead of promising access. A separate ADB raw adapter may expose only reviewed fixed service-call operations supported by shell authority and its actual marshalling limits. That is not an app-UID IBinder handle, a generic verified Parcelable codec or permission to use hwbinder. Raw connection_id is either a real connection_profiles.profile_id or reserved platform:local; object handles pin that profile, user, target and backend epoch and cannot migrate between them. HIDL declarations and completion semantics remain inventory/classification. No ordinary app backend is assumed to access hwbinder; unsupported paths report backend_unreachable:hidl. A future separately reviewed privileged backend would require an explicit scope/design change, not an inferred owner grant.

## Startup reuse and bounded admission

A new boot invalidates old admission capabilities, process-local object handles and approvals. It does not require discarding a validated semantic selection cache. Reuse is allowed only if a fresh supported capability observation matches the cache's canonical semantic facts (platform/minor/extensions/build/OEM/module/interface identity and relevant availability), scope, inventory root, catalog/overlay generations, resolver/schema version and type-graph digest. Boot ID, observation time and transient handle IDs are excluded from that semantic key, but remain new runtime evidence. Verify the app-private cache seal against the Keystore-authenticated manifest, open the immutable generation and create a new view revision bound to the new boot/capability epoch; do not mutate/relabel the old view. File identity/generation and on-read page/document hashes detect stale/corrupt data; failure quarantines the cache and closes device admission. Root/full process compromise remains outside the stated trust guarantee. Every runtime permission/reachability/wire/handle check is fresh at dispatch regardless of cache reuse.

For the API level35 (Android15) or later, 8GiB/128GB reference profile and approximately800k-entry inventory, proposed unmeasured p95 acceptance targets are <=600seconds for cold complete indexed resolution and <=10seconds for warm validated semantic reuse. Resolve in bounded batches, SQLite staging and indexed reverse-type worklists: application scratch<=64MiB, SQLite page cache<=64MiB, total service peak<=384MiB and disk scratch<=incoming catalog size. A large dependency closure that exceeds a bound spills to validated SQLite worklists or fails explicitly; it is not silently cut. Recompute affected closures on capability change, and perform full cold rebuild when compatibility keys or dependency provenance are insufficient. While Resolving, only authenticated policy/status, callback.status/callback.cancel and bindings.search/list/get are admitted; discovery reports resolving applicability. Device-affecting calls return VIEW_RESOLVING. Progress and cancellation remain bounded; the listener may be ready while device admission is unavailable, with separate status fields. These targets need real Android benchmarks; the historical Python4.30GiB/565.6second probe does not satisfy them.

## Catalog delivery and management API ownership

Large catalog delivery uses an owner-selected Storage Access Framework content URI, not the256KiB JSON request body. BridgeService obtains the owner-granted read capability, preflights capacity, streams bounded copy chunks into a new app-private staging file, hashes the exact copied bytes and fsyncs before matching the independently trusted manifest size/SHA. Only then open the SQLite input read-only for schema/integrity/FK/content validation and atomic activation. Untrusted filenames, archive paths or SQL are never commands. A bounded expiring staged-local-handle identifies this verified copy; POST /v1/catalog/imports carries that handle plus expected pins/idempotency key. An ADB-pushed file is usable only when the owner exposes it through this same supported URI flow; the app does not assume access to /data/local/tmp or another UID's private directory. Abort/quarantine incomplete or mismatched copies and never activate them.

BridgeService owns the optional /v1/catalog administration route on the same authenticated loopback listener as /mcp, with separate route authorization. It is disabled by default and enabled only by fresh local owner action for a bounded maximum10-minute window. Owner-issued credentials.kind=admin are separate from kind=mcp; admin credentials are rejected by tools/call and ordinary MCP credentials are rejected by admin routes. Admin credential expiry cannot exceed the current management window, revocation closes active admin work before the commit boundary, and every import/mutation needs its exact owner authorization and CAS rules. The local Compose facade invokes the same application service without opening HTTP or minting an admin credential. No admin route is active merely because this design contains its specification. PUT/DELETE are the mutation family; no PATCH alias is defined.

## Callback/group table and operation contracts

These tables are additions to the service configuration model. Immutable version rows have append-only history and evidence; local override revisions remain separate from imported documents. Mandatory FK checking, unique indexes, scalar/check constraints and transactional publication follow the existing SQLite contract. JSON documents are schema-validated before commit; a CHECK on JSON text alone is insufficient. The executable migration/reference integration remains a phase deliverable to validate separately.

Unknown/candidate cannot become registrable merely by a name heuristic. |

Index(client_id,state,lease_expires_at). |

callback.status input is {subscription_id?:string, renew?:boolean=false, expected_revision?:positive_integer, requested_lease_seconds?:integer}. Without an ID it lists only the authenticated client's subscriptions with bounded cursor/limit and renew=false. A single result returns state, revision, lease expiry, quota/usage, oldest/newest retained cursors, cleanup status and sanitized reason. renew=true requires an owned active subscription, expected_revision CAS and a requested duration1..300seconds, capped by the client's max_lease, original registration's approved maximum expiry and current credential/contract validity. It cannot revive closed/orphaned/unknown registrations. Missing or stale revision conflicts without renewal; extending beyond original consent requires a new explicit admission/Ask decision. callback.status is not advertised universally read-only because renew mutates lease state. callback.cancel input {subscription_id, expected_revision?, cancellation_id} is owned and idempotent, suppresses future delivery and returns delivery_closed, cleanup_confirmed/cleanup_unknown and new revision; retries never repeat an uncertain side effect blindly.

Ask is consumed once for the exact registration, event/read scope and bounded lease, not for an unlimited conversation. Event publication/reads require the current rule to remain Ask or Allow, the consumed registration-consent record/pins/lease to remain valid and the client epoch to match. No new prompt is needed per event/read. Deny, revoked credential or expired consent immediately suppresses payload and queues recorded cleanup. A renewal cannot expand that original approved scope. Pending ordinary approvals still die on restart; persisted registration consent is a consumed bounded record, not a reusable owner approval for new calls. Restart marks OS registrations orphaned while retained journal access remains subject to the still-valid explicit read consent and current policy.

Binder callback threads copy bounded typed data into a bounded broker accept queue and return promptly; synchronous local reply selection never waits for SQLite. The accept queue counts against both per-subscription and client quotas, with proposed queue cap128events/256KiB within the existing total quotas. A single worker assigns commit order and batches at most64events or16ms of queue age per transaction using synchronous=FULL, preserving security-relevant storage policy. An event becomes replayable only after commit; precommit crash loss is disclosed, and durable cursors never acknowledge uncommitted events. Async queue order is acceptance order across threads, not physical source causality. Overflow and disk failure follow the explicit loss/terminal policy; no writer wait leaks back onto Binder threads. No global SQLite durability downgrade is introduced.

The base no-query events_uri returns a bounded status document with state, oldest/newest retained cursors and the exact next-read URI template; it does not repeatedly return an old first page. Expanded cursor URIs page history. Transport SSE replay defaults to nondurable; this does not remove the separately retained application journal. Every initialized StreamableHTTP session is assigned Mcp-Session-Id, and post-initialize requests without it receive400; ordinary GET/POST/DELETE/reconnect authenticate and enforce that scope. Session expiry requires reinitialization; same-principal journal reattachment is explicit and never transfers a live callback to another principal.

## Pairing, owner authentication and boot lifecycle

Pairing uses a separate POST /pair route on the same listener, outside MCP tools and open only during a local owner's bounded pairing window. It requires the paired_tls profile: the agent pins the server fingerprint supplied through the owner-visible local QR/channel before sending any proof; reduced_http rejects pairing. A one-use server nonce plus agent nonce, fingerprint and exact proposed label hash are length-prefixed into HMAC-SHA256 under the random bootstrap secret with domain pair-v1. The secret itself is never sent. Nonces expire after60seconds, are single-use and rate-limited; the response returns the new bearer once over the pinned TLS channel. No secret/proof/credential goes to logs. Approval binds the proposed principal and fingerprint; an expired/conflicting window fails without creating an active client. This is an explicit protocol design, not an implemented cryptographic handshake claim.

Fresh local owner authentication uses Android BiometricPrompt with BIOMETRIC_STRONG or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL on the reference API35+ profile. Pairing, credential reveal/rotation, grants, admin enablement and sensitive export require a successful prompt within30seconds, bound to a single nonce, exact command, revision/target scope and current foreground activity. Ask policy may require the same mechanism by profile, with timeout/missing UI denying. If device authentication is unavailable, sensitive owner transitions remain blocked; the bridge does not weaken the profile or change device security settings. Every remote input/capture path is quiesced before protected surfaces appear and remains excluded until completion/dismissal.

The unexported boot receiver is directBootAware and handles LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED only to read the minimal nonsecret device-protected mirror and record Waiting for unlock; it performs no network, catalog migration or credential-encrypted access there. BOOT_COMPLETED/ACTION_USER_UNLOCKED reconciles the mirror against credential-encrypted desired state and requests an eligible foreground-service start. An inconsistent mirror defaults off. The selected candidate foreground-service type is specialUse with a truthful declared subtype describing the local authorized MCP binding gateway; eligibility, platform prerequisites and distribution review are release gates, not presumed approval. No connectedDevice/dataSync label is used unless the actual product behavior qualifies; unsupported start remains explicit.

Wireless-debugging endpoint discovery uses supported NsdManager/mDNS service discovery for _adb-tls-pairing._tcp and _adb-tls-connect._tcp when visible in the authorized network environment, with owner-entered host:port fallback. Same-device discovery can fail on an OEM/network and must remain an explicit state. Discovered names/ports are untrusted until TLS peer identity matches the paired ADB profile. Never scan arbitrary ports or trust a stale endpoint after boot/toggle/network change.

screen.state caps inline PNG bytes at2MiB before base64 and total JSON result at3MiB; oversized capture is explicitly downscaled with the image-to-display transform or returned as a scoped bounded resource, never silently cropped. Fixed reviewed display-selecting screencap/input variants route a captured display consistently; unsupported per-display routing is explicit. input.tap validates display ID, rotation, capture/transform freshness and bounds against the admitted target. No automatic recapture/tap or replay of an uncertain gesture is implied.

## Named Kotlin HTTP evaluation target

The evaluation candidate is official MCP Kotlin SDK0.15.0, commit76b8e7d63aac39fe41e03684e3b91a6c3724a8da, with the Ktor CIO server engine as the pure-JVM hosting candidate. The official SDK source documents StreamableHTTP integration; Ktor separately documents CIO. Neither is Android or exact2025-11-25 conformance proof. Pin the candidate's compatible Ktor/Kotlin dependency graph during the implementation spike; test initialization/session/header/SSE/resource behavior against the pinned wire baseline and reject/patch incompatible behavior rather than upgrade protocol silently. Paired HTTPS needs a verified TLS-capable Android engine/tunnel adapter; CIO support alone is not evidence of the required server TLS profile. Until that gate passes, do not ship a sensitive cleartext fallback.

LoopbackHost is the Kotlin interface owning bind/start/stop/readiness, exact listener identity and TLS configuration, Host/Origin checks, credential extraction,256KiB request/nesting limits, authenticated session routing and bounded SSE queues. McpServer owns protocol semantics above it. No engine decides authorization. The local package's Gradle build generates documentation only, not this application or SDK integration. Sources: [official SDK candidate](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/kotlin-sdk/tree/76b8e7d63aac39fe41e03684e3b91a6c3724a8da), [Ktor server engines](https://ktor.io/docs/server-engines.html).


The pinned official Settings.System reference states brightness is “between 1 (minimum) and 255 (maximum)” ([S15](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/provider/Settings.System#SCREEN_BRIGHTNESS)). This exact primary-source wording was rechecked for F-13; a reviewer's recollection of0..255 does not override it. Actual raw reads still return any observed signed32-bit value with the documented-range flag; the16..240 default write policy is a separate design restriction.

The opt-in dynamic group view uses initialization experimental capability android.bridge.toolGroups.v1 with requested mode dynamic_aliases and a server-confirmed matching capability; absent/mismatched agreement stays portable. The server additionally advertises standard tools.listChanged only when it will emit notifications/tools/list_changed. This application extension does not promise host context eviction.

# 19 Acceptance tests and delivery sequence

Build mock first, then prove the Android boundary. Passing policy tests alone does not establish compatibility, permissions, lifecycle reliability or store eligibility. Every gate produces retained test evidence and a pinned dependency manifest; there is no implementation claim in this proposal.

1	# Catalog administration contract 1.4
2	
3	This specification and `contracts/openapi.json` describe an administration API; no listener, Android bridge or HTTP handler is implemented. The offline reference models and fixture databases test contract rules. The corrected storage baseline is 1.2.0 (`user_version=3`). Prior release migrations are evidence under `../evidence/`; do not run the corrected baseline on an existing database. `tooling/migrate_v3.py` performs a checked offline copy migration to a new file. Original files remain intact.
4	
5	## Identity and authority
6	
7	`entry_id = binding_id = lowercase SHA256(UTF8(canonical_signature))`. Canonical signatures are language-prefixed source signatures defined in README, with parser-normalized types and no source/version prefix. They are not erased JVM identities. One signature in two sources has one identity and two immutable occurrences. Permission changes create declaration revisions, not new IDs. A parser canonicalization change requires an explicit identity-version migration and reviewed grant invalidation; it cannot silently retarget grants. Local additions use exactly the same derivation. Imported ID/signature mismatch is a rejected import.
8	
9	The three authorities are distinct: declared permission AST and provenance; OS runtime/backend capability; MCP client's exact binding/schema grants. CRUD changes metadata only. All generated/generic/known raw routes resolve to one canonical binding plan and policy evaluator; entry-point grants may restrict it. Known raw transaction requests must decode and validate under that schema or reject. Unknown raw requests require separate explicit broad backend/service authority and are visibly unable to enforce unknown method semantics; ordinary binding grants never imply it. Each alias carries exact schema hash, target and argument mapping hash, rechecked at admission. Unknown formats, codecs or required semantics remain visible and unavailable.
10	
11	## Registry state and publication
12	
13	SQL and JSON use `state` with staged, validated, rejected, published, retired. Create starts staged. Validation moves staged to validated or rejected. Rejected is terminal; correct bytes require a fresh immutable import ID. Publish accepts validated only, and atomically retires the old published registry, rebinds effective declarations, rebases overlays, records history/audit/outbox, increments registry generation, changes active pointer and invalidates affected approvals/schema grants. Only one published active registry is permitted by the service transaction. Re-publishing an already published registry under the same idempotency key returns the recorded result; a different key/current-active mismatch is 409. Retired cannot republish. Publication failure rolls back all changes, including generation. An import adds no active entries until publication. Validation never marks incomplete coverage complete.
14	
15	Idempotency records are scoped by authenticated admin principal plus operation and key; retain request hash, response status/body and selected resource. Same canonical request hash replays original result; reuse with different hash is 409. Stage/import verifies hashes, source provenance, identity derivation, schema major/minor support, FK/count integrity and coverage declaration before validation. No network path or arbitrary filesystem path is accepted from a caller; local_artifact_id refers to a locally registered bounded artifact.
16	
17	## Strong ETags, CAS and pagination
18	
19	One strong ETag for all current entry representations is quoted `cat1:<registry_generation>:<imported_record_sha256-or-local>:<entry_id>:<overlay_revision>:<state>`. Base rows use overlay revision 0 and state active. Hash is the canonical effective imported document hash before local changes; local entries use literal `local`. Registry generation changes whenever the selected immutable base changes. Every overlay write MUST increase that entry's revision, including state-only transitions, and append history in the same transaction. Thus any effective representation change changes this ETag. Direct SQL overlay edits outside the administration transaction are unsupported. Canonical JSON is UTF-8, sorted object keys, compact separators, no NaN/Infinity; accepted schemas disallow ambiguous nonfinite values. No weak tags, wildcard or list preconditions.
20	
21	GET by ID returns current ETag, including tombstone 410. Conflict GET is 200 with `state=conflict`, variants/base evidence and current ETag; it is never invocable. History GET is 200 with immutable history and **the current administrative ETag**, not a historical revision token. History entries' revisions are evidence only. Unknown ID is 404 without ETag. PUT/DELETE use that same current ETag even in conflict/tombstone states. Authentication/scope checks precede existence disclosure. Missing If-Match returns 428 before generic header validation; malformed precondition returns 400; stale tag returns 412 with current ETag, then transition-specific checks. This ordering is invariant across states.
22	
23	Every overlay mutation increments global overlay_generation in its transaction. Search cursors pin `(registry_id,registry_generation,overlay_generation,query_hash,last_entry_id)` and expire with 410 if either generation changed; mutable overlays are never paginated as if they were an old snapshot. Reissue the query from the start after expiry. Cursors are opaque authenticated bounded tokens, tied to the principal/query and expiry; tampered tokens are 400. Order is lexical entry_id. First and subsequent page reads pin the tuple in one read transaction. Search omits suppressed/deleted/conflict by default; administrative `include_suppressed=true` includes all three with state and ETag. Invocation discovery always omits them. A returned metadata page confers no grant.
24	
25	## Entry transitions
26	
27	| Current state | GET | POST same canonical ID | PUT with current tag | DELETE with current tag |
28	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
29	| Missing | 404 | local active, revision 1 | 404 | 404 |
30	| Imported active, no overlay | 200 | 409 | active overlay revision 1 | suppressed overlay revision 1 |
31	| Local active | 200 | 409 | active revision +1 | deleted revision +1 |
32	| Imported override active | 200 | 409 | active revision +1 | suppressed revision +1 |
33	| Suppressed imported | 410 | 409 | restore active revision +1 | idempotent 200, unchanged revision/tag |
34	| Deleted local | 410 | 409 | restore active revision +1 | idempotent 200, unchanged revision/tag |
35	| Conflict | 200 | 409 | only explicit reviewed resolution against current base hash; otherwise 409 | 409 until resolved |
36	
37	PUT never changes canonical ID or signature. `x-resolution` is required only for conflict: `{action: "rebase", expected_imported_record_sha256: "<current hash>"}`; null hash means the base is absent and explicit retain-local is selected with `action: "retain-local"`. A base-absent conflict resolves to a local active entry with the same ID; it must keep prior imported provenance in history, not a dangling imported FK. Invalid resolution or changed base returns 409; schema failures return 422. Restore requires a complete validated replacement Mutation, never an empty PATCH. A local addition followed by import of the same signature is always marked conflict during publication even if bytes happen to match. An import followed by local POST is 409. Neither path silently replaces or merges provenance. Upstream unchanged base preserves overlay; changed/missing base marks conflict, including suppression tombstones, so deletion intent and evidence remain auditable. No physical imported/history deletion occurs in CRUD.
38	
39	Local override documents preserve reserved identity/provenance fields; API accepts only Mutation fields and constructs origin/state/registry_version/revisions itself. Sources and raw imported evidence are never editable via PUT. Imported provenance cannot be fabricated by local clients. Admin authentication uses a separate owner-authorized scope; ordinary MCP device grants cannot call this API. Concurrent compare/update happens inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction with an affected-row/CAS check and audit/history append before commit. Unknown schema major/required semantics returns 422. All failures leave state/generations unchanged.
40	
41	## Deliverable boundary and coverage
42	
43	The generator emits a searchable complete inventory of acquired declarations, including unsupported/unreachable entries and reasons. It does not assert universal discovery of private/OEM surfaces. AIDL ordinals and declared method IDs are evidence, never wire transaction codes without generated/compiler proof. Public binding/permission coverage is measured against source inventories by namespace/version/kind and unresolved records; absent annotation is unknown. Source task owns acquisition/current production imports; release-002's 135,508 records and earlier pre-import 0 records are different frozen states. Source completeness remains an overall acceptance blocker until an independent current review establishes otherwise. Namespace/package modules plus global indexes/permissions/types/evidence/overrides remain a proposal; no semantic re-sharding is performed here.
44	
45	
46	## Registry and identity implementation details
47	
48	The corrected schema supports several immutable registries in one database through registry_entries(registry_id,entry_id). effective_entries is an active-registry view, not a mutable/stored document or ETag table. Builder input must contain catalog.registry_version (positive monotonic publication number), android_version, api_level and coverage; each source explicitly supplies api_level (null when unknown) and channel. A new standalone release seeds registry_generation from registry_version. The serving publisher rejects a new registry_version not greater than its active version, except exact idempotent replay. Cursor tokens also include registry_id, so replacement of a file or a selected source set cannot revive an old cursor. In-database switches increment generation atomically. The builder only publishes its private staging database after all gates; transient staged pointers in that private file are never exposed to serving readers.
49	
50	idempotency_records is the sole administration replay store, keyed by verified principal, operation and key. legacy_import_jobs contains unscoped historical prototype receipts copied from storage v2; these can never authorize replay of an authenticated API operation. registry_events and registry_outbox preserve publication/approval-invalidation evidence. The bridge and catalog DDL coexist in one transaction domain for serving publication. Storage user_version2 is the immutable original release-002 baseline; v3 is created only through a checked offline copy or a new build.
51	
52	Dispatch manifests carry schema_hash (canonical identity, kind, arguments, return type and codec identity/status), permission_hash and document_hash separately. Provenance-only additions leave schema_hash stable. Publication still invalidates grants and approvals for changed permission_hash, required semantics, argument mapping, backend authority or target constraints even when schema_hash is unchanged: delete/disable the affected client binding rules in the same policy-revision transaction before the new mapping becomes usable. No document or metadata edit grants authority.
53	
54	External annotation permission_relations.line is a one-based XML item ordinal, not an XML source line; raw_annotation preserves original item name, archive member and annotation values through annotation_evidence locators. Malformed XML is retained as an annotation-xml issue and the source report becomes partial. Declaration/parameter/unmatched annotation cases are fixture-tested. Unknown/unsupported semantics remain noninvocable.
55	
56	Current source evidence identity scheme3 hashes an acquisition object (URL, revision, SHA-256, retrieval timestamp, path, API applicability, channel, kind, license and scope) plus a processing fingerprint of the extractor, parser helpers and Entry/permission contracts. source_details records x-source-identity-version=3 and x-processing-sha256. A parser correction therefore creates new immutable derived-evidence occurrences without fabricating a retrieval time or overwriting an earlier declaration. Stable binding/entry IDs remain independent of acquisition and processing identity. Historical source schemes1/2 remain preserved by copy migration. Registry IDs hash both source-set identity and explicit catalog metadata.
57	
58	Canonicalization scheme2 reserves `java:package:<qualified-name>` for package inventory nodes, avoiding collision with `java:<qualified-type>` when one source set contains both a type and an identically named package. Type/member source signatures retain their existing form. This is an explicit canonicalization correction: old immutable catalog documents and hashes remain untouched, old package overlay/grant keys are not automatically aliased or retargeted, and publication must quarantine any identity-kind ambiguity until owner reconciliation. Package nodes are discovery-only and never executable. `test_package_and_type_have_distinct_identity_namespaces` reproduces and guards the collision.
59	
60	When an upstream base entry disappears and no overlay exists, it is absent from the new selected view rather than a synthetic conflict. Its old registry/declaration evidence remains immutable. Existing local changes or suppression tombstones instead enter explicit conflict on changed/missing base. Registry identity/document validation must complete before any selected-view mutation; rejected publication preserves pointer, entries and cursor generations.
61	
62	
63	## Publication/storage enforcement and aggregation
64	
65	Only one registry may be published. active_registry has immediate admission triggers and a deferred composite FK to the published registry state; retiring the old registry and selecting the new one occur in a single transaction, so a retired pointer cannot commit. The builder validates private registry_entries before publishing and installs its active pointer only afterward. Every overlay revision has a deferred FK to the same entry_history revision, forcing history presence at commit; JSON validity is checked in storage and full Entry/Mutation schemas are checked by the service. Active local/import collisions must become explicit conflicts before pointer publication; runtime discovery joins overlays by stable entry_id and never emits duplicate IDs. Failed publication rolls back entries, state, pointer, history and generations.
66	
67	The permission aggregate is positive declared-evidence discovery, not a universal claim for every source version or an OS grant. A plain absence of a recognized annotation is excluded when selecting a single positive requirement; it is never explicit-none. In mixed positive/absent or differing-evidence cases, extensions.permission_variants retains each AST with x-occurrences and x-absence-of-annotation where applicable. Invocation still resolves the exact target/source/schema and live OS authority; it may not infer no permission from absence or use the aggregate to widen client grants. An unresolved/conflicting positive expression makes the aggregate unknown.
68	
69	RawGrant.schema.json is the closed scope-only contract for constraints_json (allowed_targets, allowed_handles, allowed_displays, max_items). Connection/descriptor/code range/flag mask/hash/effect live only in SQL columns; duplicate keys in constraints_json are rejected. ImportRequest carries registry_version and coverage before staging validation. Generated aliases and binding.invoke share policy_tool_id binding.invoke; wrappers retain additional restrictive rules.
70	
71	
72	Pointer admission rejects active or suppressed imported overlays whose base_record_hash is missing or differs from the target registry entry. The publication transaction marks those overlays conflict and appends history before selecting the new pointer; tombstones are included. User Mutation.reason is stored in entry_history_reasons and returned as HistoryEvent.reason (legacy/system absence allowed). The sidecar shares entry/revision FK and is append-only; the service inserts both rows in the same transaction. A null Registry.api_level means unknown applicability, not an inferred API level. permission_reader.read demonstrates future-node quarantine while builder-generated ASTs remain strictly validated.
73	
74	## Startup device-resolved bindings and types (additive contract 1.3)
75	
76	`DeviceResolution.schema.json` specifies internally collected facts, inventory variants, resolved rows and immutable snapshot headers. The offline `device_resolution.py` is an executable reference over fixture facts; no device collector, Android Binder engine or HTTP service is implemented here. The complete versioned inventory is retained even when an entry is unavailable or unknown on the connected device. Historical/future SDK records must therefore be retained as inventory evidence; the existing current-target SDK-index projection is insufficient as the sole resolver input. Full production import of the normalized availability metadata remains an explicit release gate.
77	
78	The collector records platform major/minor separately from SDK extension levels, OEM/build identity, observable installed module versions and supported interface version/hash/reachability evidence. It must not infer a minor version, extension, private interface or permission grant from an API major alone. Denied/unreachable/unsupported probes produce unknown; authoritative absence produces unavailable. Source-backed applicability alternatives are OR clauses, each containing AND predicates. Binding and type variants use the same evaluator. An unresolved possible variant with incompatible schema or dependencies keeps selection unknown. Type dependencies must name available type rows with the exact selected schema hash; missing or conflicting types cannot silently select a codec. Known recursive type components are resolved consistently. Availability is separate from OS/backend authority and MCP client policy, which are rechecked before dispatch.
79	
80	`GET /v1/catalog/device-views/current?profile_id=...&target_key=...` returns a bounded status/header and an ETag. Before first activation the header is null and view generation is zero; this bootstrap state still has a valid ETag. `GET /v1/catalog/device-views/{view_id}` returns the immutable small header, not the entire inventory. `GET /v1/catalog/device-views/{view_id}/entries` returns at most 500 rows with all/available/unavailable/unknown filtering. A cursor binds the immutable view, authorized reader, profile/target, filter and page boundary; invalidation or expiry returns410. Historical headers remain evidence and cannot authorize dispatch. Authorization is checked before disclosing existence or scope.
81	
82	The current-view strong ETag is `"dv2:<scope_sha256>:<view_generation>:<capability_epoch>:<catalog_generation>:<overlay_generation>:<inventory_sha256>"`. `scope_sha256` hashes the canonical JSON array `[profile_id,target_key,android_user_id,backend_instance_id,device_instance_id]`; it is an opaque scope identity, not credentials. Counters are decimal nonnegative integers bounded by the schema. A stale view has the new epoch and therefore a different token even before the replacement activates. `POST /v1/catalog/device-views/refresh` is restricted to the authenticated local owner and a configured profile/target. It accepts only that profile/target and one exact strong If-Match from the current-status read, never asserted facts or arbitrary probe instructions. After authorization, missing/malformed/mismatching preconditions return428/400/412 respectively, including the generation-zero bootstrap. A matched request atomically invalidates admission and queues the bounded internal refresh, returning202 with current status. Repeated or concurrent requests must re-read the new token; none can activate a snapshot built for an old epoch.
83	
84	Startup, reconnect and relevant device/build/module/extension/interface/backend/catalog changes invalidate the selected view. Capture, resolution, dependency validation and hash sealing happen against one fact epoch and pinned catalog/overlay generation. Publication is a single SQLite transaction comparing the scope, current generation, epoch and catalog pins before switching the active pointer; failure preserves the old immutable snapshot as stale evidence. Dispatch pins the selected schema/type-graph/view and checks freshness again at admission. The reference `ViewStore` is a single-thread state-machine oracle for this contract; a runtime requires a real transaction/lock and integration tests. View retention, quota and garbage collection follow the bounded derived-view policy in the design. No app monitoring scheduler is added.
85	
86	Storage additionally rejects deletion of `active_registry` and `catalog_view` singletons and malformed lowercase SHA-256 values in imported binding IDs, source digests, registry-entry hashes and nullable overlay base hashes. `overlay_etags` is the executable cat1 projection for all overlay states, including tombstones and conflicts; its base component is the currently selected imported hash or `local` when the new selected base is absent. The old immutable base hash remains separate conflict evidence.
87	
88	
89	## Producer-to-inventory projection and executable device storage
90	
91	`catalog_projection.py` enriches only derived registry entries; immutable binding_declarations and source bytes remain unchanged. `registry_inventory` contains one validated InventoryEntity per registry entry, sealed with the registry. Its variants use `dispatch_manifest.contract_digest`, contract format3, shared by generated aliases and generic dispatch schema pins. Source locators and permission metadata never establish a codec. Semantic type references and declared structured-type shapes contribute to the contract; changing this digest version requires explicit schema/grant reconciliation and does not silently retarget existing grants.
92	
93	The SDK index producer now emits every historical, current, future and unknown-lifecycle record. `excluded_history_or_future` is retained only as a compatibility diagnostic for the native current-target projection; it no longer means records were omitted. Only `lifecycle_status=current-at-target` enters current exact-index annotation/JVM-equivalence lookup. This flag describes the frozen native SDK target, never a device extension observation or runtime authority. Raw member and container lifecycle attributes remain separate. Parsed `sdks` pairs use SDK ID0 for platform versions and declared nonzero SDK IDs for extension minima. Omitted member `sdks` inherits the container value because the public Metalava writer suppresses identical attributes; explicit member pairs replace that set. The containing type dependency enforces its independent lifetime. Unknown SDK IDs/syntax remain unknown with raw evidence. [Metalava source](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/tools/metalava/+/a9d285ca63f95134ff1eb2c02eff5638109a5ad3%5E2..a9d285ca63f95134ff1eb2c02eff5638109a5ad3/) documents the pair format and inheritance.
94	
95	An index supplies introduced-inclusive/removed-exclusive ranges and separately evidenced extension alternatives. A source occurrence without an index proves only its explicit major.minor point, represented by `platform_point:[major,minor]`. A point match is available evidence; every other major/minor (including an unknown minor) is unknown with PLATFORM_APPLICABILITY_UNPROVEN. A point never fabricates a removal bound. An API major alone never proves a minor or a whole-major range. Metadata remains unknown when no source-supported rule exists. Reference fields resolve only a unique declared type in the same repository/revision/platform snapshot with package/nesting/import evidence. Intrinsic primitive/array leaves are explicit TypeReference.status=primitive and remain codec-unknown. Generic, wildcard, absent or ambiguous schemas remain unknown. Required unresolved type evidence is an AND-unknown predicate, so a proven version exclusion still yields unavailable. Containing types, argument/return types and structured-field schemas are dependencies; each pins the exact type contract hash. Full source/shape/evidence variants remain visible.
96	
97	The builder streams `device_inventory.jsonl` and its versioned manifest, validates each InventoryEntity, enforces one-to-one entry counts, and includes the inventory metadata in the derived entry document hash. Older releases/copy migrations without this projection cannot supply a complete startup inventory; startup must reject an absent/incomplete inventory rather than inventing it. The inventory contract is DeviceResolution2.1.0: the additive platform_point key changes applicability semantics and requires explicit version handling. Resolved snapshots/Facts use DeviceView3.0.0: base contract_hash and transitive graph_digest produce the final schema_hash used by client grants. Earlier resolved drafts cannot activate silently. Previous draft snapshots remain historical evidence and are rejected for activation; no silent migration is defined. Existing Entry1.1 and catalog storage1.2 envelopes are unchanged. OpenAPI specification version is1.4.0.
98	
99	`bridge-config.sql` now stores scoped epoch-bound capability facts, immutable staged/sealed device_views and device_view_entries, an active pointer with exact generation/epoch/catalog/overlay CAS, and append-only invalidation reasons. A catalog-pinned inventory_sha256 (canonical sorted InventoryEntity JSONL digest) and expected_inventory_count prevent partial or substituted inventories from activating. The trusted loader validates the complete inventory before sealing device_inventory_sets/members. Activation recomputes resolution from that pinned inventory/facts and rejects substituted members, contract hashes, dependencies or states. SQLite independently checks sealed inventory membership, selected base contracts and dependency pins; core SQLite has no built-in SHA256, so the offline loader verifies content hashes before sealing. `device_view_storage.py` is the offline SQLite transaction reference: validate the snapshot/facts/hash/type closure, write all rows, seal membership, then compare-and-switch inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Facts carry capability_epoch and observed_at; the resolver and publisher both reject old-epoch facts. Per-row graph_digest hashes the sorted transitive root/type `(entry_id,contract_hash)` closure and is rechecked at publication. `binding_availability` is a read-only fresh-active-view projection; `resolved_device_catalog` includes bindings and types. Neither grants permission. Wire mapping proof is versioned in binding_wire_contracts, separately from existence; unknown codecs/contracts cannot be invoked. Retention requires explicit maintenance and rejects active/pinned view deletion. No Android collector, Binder service, MCP service or HTTP deployment is implemented.
100	
101	Resolved3 schema identity is SHA256(canonical `{schema_format:"closure3",contract_hash:C,graph_digest:G}`); G hashes the sorted transitive entry/base-contract pairs, including the root. This makes a dependent type change invalidate previous binding schema grants without cyclic hash recursion. Raw lifecycle/annotation headers stay in provenance and are excluded from semantic type shape hashes. Formal type variables never resolve to similarly named package/java.lang classes.
102	
103	Strong status ETag syntax is `"dv2:<scope_sha256>:<generation>:<capability_epoch>:<catalog_generation>:<overlay_generation>:<inventory_sha256>"`; an uninitialized fixture store uses SHA256(canonical null) as the inventory token and cannot publish until it has a trusted inventory. All counters are canonical decimal. Inaccessible historical view/header and entry-list requests both return404 after authentication. Internal Device schemas are marked x-internal and are not request payloads.
104	
105	A verified wire row must provide object codecs with nonempty codec_id and matching final schema_hash, plus nonempty evidence. The tuple (binding,schema,descriptor,transaction_code,nullable-interface-version) is unique; transaction codes/flags are uint32. These structural checks do not verify codec implementation or confer invocation authority: only a trusted adapter with complete proven ABI/layout may admit the row. Unknown/unsupported proof states remain visible.
106	
107	Semantic contract format3 normalizes structured field/supertype references without their proof prose/source revision metadata, retains type parameters and declared supertypes, and includes parameter directions, known wire type annotations, oneway metadata and HIDL result types. Permission/lifecycle provenance remains separate. All hashes are versioned inputs to closure3; format2 grants/codecs are never silently migrated to new schema hashes. Unknown type/import/compiler/ABI semantics still prevent typed invocation.
108	
109	The runtime input is effective_device_inventory.capture, taken under one read transaction and exact registry/catalog/overlay generation pins. It preserves every base, local, suppressed/conflict/deleted node. catalog_state/catalog_revision are independent of three-state version existence and per-client permission. Local additions lack positive applicability unless supported by imported evidence; no version is invented. Structured field overrides update their enclosing type and transitive schema hashes. Effective catalog_document_sha256 pins the canonical selected Entry metadata (independent of semantic schema hash); generated aliases reject stale documents and the offline known-route policy gate composes availability, whole-graph catalog exposure, current document pins and canonical client/OS authority decisions. The capture digest is over the effective inventory, including local state/revisions/document pins; the immutable producer manifest remains the base inventory digest. Global catalog edits invalidate views even when a metadata edit leaves the semantic schema hash stable.
110	
111	The materializing Python oracle is an offline validation implementation, not the Android memory architecture. The exact historical008-scale checkpoint is retained with code hashes:799527entities,565.6seconds full resolution/validation,4.30GiB whole-probe peak. Later contract3/overlay changes are not retroactively measured. Runtime resolution stages complete results in indexed SQLite, uses available-edge/reverse indexes and bounded worklists/closure traversal, streams canonical hashes with bounded scratch storage, and activates only after complete checks. No Android performance or full799527-row SQLite activation is claimed.
112	
113	Wire tuple identity is immutable/unique; evidence acquisition is separately append-only. wire_proof_revisions records complete versioned proof/codecs under the existing tuple, wire_proof_active selects a revision with next-revision CAS, and current_wire_proofs exposes either the selected revision or the immutable initial proof as revision0. Unknown proof can become verified, be superseded or be revoked to unknown/unsupported without rewriting history, changing semantic client schema grants or inventing a different tuple. Verified revisions require matching schema codecs and nonempty evidence. Admission/Ask pins the selected proof record_sha256 and revision, then rechecks selection immediately before dispatch; a changed/revoked proof invalidates that pending plan. This structural fixture does not verify an actual ABI: the trusted adapter must still verify endpoint/profile/device/interface/OEM compatibility and full codec implementation before invocation. No HTTP/MCP proof-write endpoint or Android operation is implemented.
114

# Catalog administration contract 1.4

This specification and `contracts/openapi.json` describe an administration API; no listener, Android bridge or HTTP handler is implemented. The offline reference models and fixture databases test contract rules. The corrected storage baseline is 1.2.0 (`user_version=3`). Prior release migrations are evidence under `../evidence/`; do not run the corrected baseline on an existing database. `tooling/migrate_v3.py` performs a checked offline copy migration to a new file. Original files remain intact.

## Identity and authority

`entry_id = binding_id = lowercase SHA256(UTF8(canonical_signature))`. Canonical signatures are language-prefixed source signatures defined in README, with parser-normalized types and no source/version prefix. They are not erased JVM identities. One signature in two sources has one identity and two immutable occurrences. Permission changes create declaration revisions, not new IDs. A parser canonicalization change requires an explicit identity-version migration and reviewed grant invalidation; it cannot silently retarget grants. Local additions use exactly the same derivation. Imported ID/signature mismatch is a rejected import.

All generated/generic/known raw routes resolve to one canonical binding plan and policy evaluator; entry-point grants may restrict it. Rejected is terminal; correct bytes require a fresh immutable import ID. Publish accepts validated only, and atomically retires the old published registry, rebinds effective declarations, rebases overlays, records history/audit/outbox, increments registry generation, changes active pointer and invalidates affected approvals/schema grants. Publication failure rolls back all changes, including generation. An import adds no active entries until publication. Validation never marks incomplete coverage complete.

Idempotency records are scoped by authenticated admin principal plus operation and key; retain request hash, response status/body and selected resource. Same canonical request hash replays original result; reuse with different hash is 409. Stage/import verifies hashes, source provenance, identity derivation, schema major/minor support, FK/count integrity and coverage declaration before validation. No network path or arbitrary filesystem path is accepted from a caller; local_artifact_id refers to a locally registered bounded artifact.

## Strong ETags, CAS and pagination
